docs.title: Awarding XP:
docs.text:
• XP will not just be awarded for defeating enemies combat, but also for the following
  • Completing Quests (main or side quests)
  • Engaging with the story events
  • Social Encounters
  • Puzzles
  • Avoiding combat or causing the enemies to flee
  • Saving Shared Destiny points (see inspiration)
  • If you miss a session, you will not gain the XP for that session, unless you write a story about what your character was doing and how they also gained XP while away from the group. This story must be read aloud at the start of the next session.

docs.title: Class Tradeoffs:
docs.text:
• If you would like to take on an extra challenge or give your character more flavor, I have made the following “tradeoff” options. These make your character more interesting or powerful in some aspect, but come with a heavy roleplay cost. This is only advised for more experienced players. These are merely suggestions, feel free to ask to use a different class’s trade off or create an entirely new one. Make sure to talk to me before applying or picking any of these.
  • Artificer: “Costs an arm and a leg”
  • You can have 1 extra infusion active at a time, given that it replaces one of your lost limbs.
  • Barbarian: “Uncontrollable Rage”
  • You no longer need to track the number of rages you have available. When you Rage, you must make a Wisdom saving throw with a DC equal to 10 + your Proficiency Bonus. Failing causes you to be uncontrollable, attacking the nearest creature within 60 feet of you until your rage ends.
  • Bard: “Fame”
  • While not the most famous bard, you have made somewhat of a name for yourself. At times, people will ask to talk with you, or for you to sign something of theirs. This comes with favors and small perks from those that like your work, but it also comes with heavy scrutiny and infamy from those who dislike you.
  • Cleric: “Fanatical”
  • You are a loyal and devout follower of your deity. You gain Expertise in Religion checks, as you have studied your holy books from cover to cover. As a result, you must uphold your deities teaching to the letter of the law. Any deviations, and you risk losing your faith or incurring divine punishment.
  • Druid: “Animalistic”
  • You can learn up to 8 animal forms at a time. However, when you are Bloodied when in animal form, you become uncontrolled and animalistic. You must behave as that animal would and you can only communicate as that animal would until your wildshape ends.
  • Fighter: “Master of One”
  • You have specialized in one type of weapon. Instead of using mastery properties for multiple weapons, you instead use the mastery of just one type of weapon. When you do so, you gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls with that weapon. Additionally you can add either the Push or Vex properties to the chosen weapon. You may only activate one mastery property at a time with this feature. You may not use mastery properties of any other weapon and you have a -1 to attack and damage rolls with other weapons.
  • Monk: “Nonviolence”
  • You have taken an oath of nonviolence, and will avoid confrontation at all costs. Whenever you drop a creature to 0 hit points with your attacks, it falls unconscious rather than dying outright. You cannot initiate a fight, and you cannot call others to strike in your stead. Due to this oath, you are well respected and have advantage on checks to negotiate peace and diplomacy.
  • Paladin: “Divine Responsibility”
  • Your divine sense is always active, and it can detect the presence of moral evil, not just special creatures. When you detect evil though, you must snuff it out, at all costs, no matter how powerful your foe is.
  • Ranger: “Wildborn”
  • You are extremely comfortable in the wild, gaining Advantage on all social checks while out in the wilderness. This includes checks to interact with animals, woodland creatures, or other forest dwellers. Alternatively, you are uncomfortable in large cities, gaining Disadvantage on all social checks when in large cities.
  • Rogue: “The Sense”
  • You can sense when someone is watching you, with the feeling growing more intense based on how closely you are being tracked. This has the downside of making you paranoid. If you are ever on guard or on watch alone, you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw with a DC equal to 10 + your Proficiency Bonus, or freak out and become incapable of doing meaningful work until you finish a Short or Long Rest. While freaking out, you have Disadvantage on all ability checks and attack rolls.
  • Sorcerer: “Blood magic”
  • When you cast a spell with material components, you can instead use your body as the material component. If it has a gold piece cost, you must sacrifice a 1 hit point for every 10 gold that the component costs. After doing so, your hit point maximum is reduced by that amount until you finish a long rest. This rule applies to any material components with a listed gold piece cost, whether or not they are consumed.
  • Warlock: “On Call”
  • You have secured a very personal and strict contract with your patron. You can communicate with them directly, during a Short or Long Rest. They can give you advice or information, but anytime they need you, you must obey their commands and instructions, lest you break their pact.
  • Wizard: “Eccentric”
  • You spend much more time around books than you do around people. You have a +1 to all Intelligence checks but a -1 to all Charisma checks.

docs.title: Resting:
docs.text:
Short rests take 8 hours, 6 of which must be dedicated to sleep. The other 2 hours can be dedicated to light activity such as reading, taking watch, crafting, etc.

Long rests may only happen in designated areas such as towns, settlements, or fortified structures and take 24 hours of sleep and light activity. Light activity consists of any activity that is not too demanding on the adventurer. Socializing, shopping, studying, and crafting are some examples of light activity. A Long Rest is broken if you cast a level 1+ spell, engage in combat, or leave the settlement you are resting in. If a Long Rest is broken, the character gains the benefits of a Short Rest if at least 8 hours have already passed during the rest.

Based on the location, there is a certain GP cost per person to rest. This is a combination of food, lodging, and any other expenses, such as stables for horses. This cost is location specific, and usually depends on the wealth of the location and the amenities provided.

Due to the lengthier rest time, any ability or spell which lasts for 8 hours will instead last until the next long rest. One prominent example of this is the Mage Armor spell.

docs.title: Critical Hits:
docs.text:
• Normal damage + maximum of the damage dice. Describe critical hits for extra effect
  • For example: if you are using a greatsword, and have +3 STR, you will deal 2d6 + 3 + 12 (max of 2d6) on a critical hit
  • Special effects when you crit (choose 1)
  • Groin shot/Trip
  • Prone and loses action next turn
  • Sever limb
  • The target loses either a leg or an arm
  • Leg: Halved movement
  • Arm: Disadvantage on strength and dexterity based attacks, ability checks and saving throws
  • If the creature is using one of its limbs for attacks, it loses the relevant attack
  • EG: if the creature is an owlbear, severing one of it’s libs removes it’s claw attack
  • Vital hit
  • The target instantly loses concentration on any spells or abilities
  • The target loses access to one of its abilities
  • The target bleeds for a number of rounds equal to the ability modifier used for the attack (1d4 damage per round)
  • Disarm
  • Target must use an action(and possibly some movement) to retrieve their weapon
  • If the target uses natural weapons such as claws, refer to sever limb
  • Head
  • Blinded or Deafened indefinitely
  • Stunned until the end of the attacker’s next turn
  • Extras up to player imagination and judged by DM discretion

docs.title: Death Saves:
docs.text: • Death saves are kept secret (Only the dying player and the DM know). Please refrain from hinting at what the result was.

docs.title: Falling:
docs.text: Whenever a creature would fall 10 ft or more, the creature could choose to delay its fall until the end of its next turn, or the end of its current turn, whichever comes first (a.k.a Coyote Time). When a creature hits the ground it takes 1d6 damage for every 10ft that it falls up to a maximum of 150d6. A creature falls 500 ft per round unless slowed by magic or some special ability.

docs.title: Flanking:
docs.text:
• Flanking an enemy grants a +2 to attack rolls. To count as flanking a creature, at least one of its allies must be adjacent to an enemy and on opposite sides or corners of the enemy’s space.
  • When in doubt about whether two creatures flank an enemy on a grid, trace an imaginary line between the centers of the creatures’ spaces. If the line passes through opposite sides or corners of the enemy’s space, the enemy is flanked.

docs.title: Potions:
docs.text:
• Most potions can be used or administered as an action
  • Healing potions use the following rules:
  • Using a bonus action:
  • Roll Healing as normal
  • Imagine “Shotgunning” the potion
  • Cannot Administer a healing potion as a bonus action.
  • Using an action
  • Take the maximum number for the dice roll
  • Administering a potion requires an action, but grants the full healing

docs.title: Pushing Creatures Into Walls and Other Solid Objects
docs.text:
• If a creature is moved by a spell or ability into a wall or another creature, it takes damage proportional to the remaining amount they would have been pushed. For each 5 extra feet the creature would have been pushed, it takes 1d4 bludgeoning damage. If the creature is pushed into another creature, both creatures take the full damage.
  • Example 1: A battlemaster fighter uses pushing attack to push an enemy goblin backwards. The goblin flies 5 feet backwards and then hits a solid wall. Since the goblin would have moved 10 more feet if the wall wasn’t there, he instead takes 2d4 bludgeoning damage.
  • Example 2: A Warlock uses a repelling blast to push a zombie into the necromancer standing 5 feet behind it. The zombie flies back 5 feet and then hits the necromancer. Since the zombie would have traveled 5 more feet both the necromancer and the zombie each take 1d4 bludgeoning damage.

docs.title: Sweep/Cleave attacks:
docs.text: • When you reduce a creature to zero hit points with a weapon attack, you can divert any remaining damage to an additional creature of your choice, provided you are proficient with the weapon and your initial attack roll also hits the chosen creature. For melee weapon attacks, the target must be in reach. For ranged weapon attacks: Target must be in range and in a straight line

docs.title: Spell Rulings:
docs.text:
• Counterspell and Dispel Magic will be run using the following method
  • If the spell being countered is equal to or less than the level of the spell slot used for counterspell, the original spell has no effect and the action used to cast it is wasted, along with any resource or spell slot used is wasted.
  • If the spell being countered is greater than the level of the spell slot used for counterspell, then the counterspell caster must make a check using their spell casting ability (no proficiency) against a DC = 10 + the spells level. The counterspeller can gain a bonus to this check equal to the level of spell slot above 3 that they use to cast counterspell.
  • For example, if a wizard is trying to counter a level 5 Cone of Cold spell with a level 4 Counterspell, the wizard has to roll a d20 + their Intelligence modifier + 1 (for using a 4th level spell slot, which is one above 3). The wizard would need to beat a DC of 15, which is 10 + 5 (the level of the spell)
  • Inflict wounds
  • We will use the 2014 version of this spell

docs.title: Spell Durations:
docs.text: • Any spell lasting 8 hours will now instead last until the next long rest

docs.title: Spell Scrolls:
docs.text: Anyone can use spell scrolls regardless of class, but doing so might have unintended side effects. If the spell scroll being used is not on your class list, then make an Arcana check. The DC for this check is 10 + the spell’s level. If you roll 10 less than the DC, a wild magic surge is triggered. If your roll is 10 higher than the spell’s DC, the spell is cast and the spell scroll can be used again.

docs.title: Stealth:
docs.text:
• A stealth operation happens in multiple phases. Most operations start in the hidden phase. Some may start in the searching phase, if the enemy is expecting the party:
  • Hidden
  • The group makes a group stealth check as they are moving around, if the group check beats the passive perception of the enemy, they continue unnoticed. Otherwise, the enemy begins to search.
  • If the party is infiltrating, or is unexpected, they start here
  • Searching
  • The enemy is not fully aware of your presence, but they begin to make perception checks to try and figure out what the disturbance is. The group rerolls a group stealth check contested with the enemy’s group perception check. Failing causes the enemy to see you.
  • If the party is escaping a group of enemies, they start in this phase
  • Seen
  • The enemy notices the group and acts accordingly
  • Surprise
  • If the group attacks before the seen phase, they get surprise against the enemy (see surprise in the combat section)

docs.title: Morale Checks:
docs.text:
• The DM may choose to do a morale check when the enemies are outnumbered, surprised, or losing numbers quickly. Have the leader of the enemies (or the most powerful if they are unorganized) make a Wisdom check. If the check equals or exceeds the DC, the enemies pass the morale check and continue to fight. The DC is calculated using the following formula, but may have additional modifiers based on the situation.
  • DC = 10 - # of enemies alive + # of players that are not unconscious.
  • Any additional situation modifiers should be applied using the following rule: Any positive modifiers make it more difficult for the enemies to stick around, while negative modifiers make it easier for the enemies to stick around. Examples are listed below
Situation Modifier The enemies were surprised +1 The enemies have lost a key combatant +2 The players passed an intimidation check against the enemies +1 The players landed a critical hit +1 The players were surprised -1 The enemies landed a critical hit -1 The enemies are significantly stronger than the players -3 The enemies are significantly weaker than the players +3

docs.title: Weapon sizes:
docs.text:
• Damage dice progression when increasing size
  • 1 > 1d4 > 1d6 > 1d8/2d4 > 1d10 > 1d12/2d6 > 2d8 > 2d10 > 2d12 > 3d8
  • When using an oversized weapon you have disadvantage on attacks with that weapon if you are one size smaller than the creature it was designed for. If you are two sizes smaller, then you are not able to wield such a large weapon. Additionally if you grow or shrink in size possibly due to an enlarge/reduce spell, your weapon damage increases by one size for every size category you go up. When you shrink your weapon damage also goes down by one size for every size category you shrink.
  • Your reach increases by 5ft for every size category you go up and decreases to a minimum of 5ft for every size category you shrink.

docs.title: Casting Multiple Spells on a Turn:
docs.text:
• Note: This is actually identical to the default rules in 2024, thus moved to archive
  • A caster can cast multiple spells on a turn if they meet any of the following requirements
  • Players: Only one spell uses a spell slot
  • EX: A druid casting Spike growth (action) and a shillelagh (bonus action)
  • EX: A drow cleric casting healing word (bonus action) and using the darkness spell (action) from their species features.

docs.title: Overcharge
docs.text:
General Feat (Prerequisite: Level 8+)

You gain the following benefits.

Ability Score Increase. Increase your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

Stamina Drain. When you use either Spell Chucker or Destruction, you gain one level of exhaustion for each ability used.

Spell Chucker. When you take the Magic action to cast a level 1+ spell, you can use your Bonus Action to cast a level 1+ spell that also has a casting time of 1 action. The spell you cast as a Bonus Action must be at least 1 level lower than the initial spell cast. This ability ignores the restriction on only using 1 spell slot per turn.

Destruction. When you cast a spell that deals damage, you can choose to do maximum damage with a spell, but trigger a Wild Magic Surge and take half the damage you deal

docs.title: Size Doesn't Matter
docs.text:
General Feat (Prerequisite: Level 4+)

You gain the following benefits.

Ability Score Increase. Increase your Strength or Constitution score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

Powerful Build. You count as one size larger when grappling, determining your carrying capacity, and how much you can push lift or drag

Large Size. You can cast Enlarge/Reduce on yourself without expending a spell slot. Once you cast that spell in this way, you must complete a long rest before using this trait again.

docs.title: Weapon Expert
docs.text:
General Feat (Prerequisite: Level 8+, The ability to use the mastery property of at least one kind of weapon)

You gain the following benefits.

Ability Score Increase. Increase your Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution score by 1, to a maximum of 20.

Power Strike. Before you make a melee attack with a weapon that you can use the mastery property for, you can choose to take a -3 penalty to the attack roll. If the attack hits, you add +1d10 to the attack's damage.

Relentless. When you hit with a weapon that you can use the mastery property for, you can activate the Vex or Sap mastery property in addition to a different mastery property you’re using with that weapon.

docs.title: Gunner (for cowboy rules only)
docs.text:
General Feat (Prerequisite: Level 4+, Proficiency in Firearms)

Ability Score Increase. Increase your Dexterity by 1 to a maximum of 20

Quickdraw. You ignore the Loading and Special Reload properties of firearms.

Deadeye. As a Bonus Action, you can focus your aim until the end of your turn. When you do so, you gain a +1d4 bonus to attack and damage rolls with Firearms.

High Noon. You learn the Tumbleweed cantrip. Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma is your spellcasting ability for it.

Casting Time: Action

Range: 60 feet

As you strike with your weapon, you weave a phantom image around it, extending the weapon’s reach. Make one attack with the weapon, when you do so, your reach is increased by 5 feet for this attack.

docs.title: 4th-level Conjuration Spell (Bard, Sorcerer, Warlock, Wizard)
docs.text:
Casting Time: Action

Range: 60 feet

Component: V

Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute

You conjure an Iron Maiden around a creature you can see within range. The target must make a Strength saving throw or take 4d10 piercing damage and be trapped in the Iron Maiden. While trapped, the target has the Blinded and Restrained conditions. While trapped the creature has total cover from every direction and takes 2d10 piercing damage at the start of each of its turns. At the end of each of its turns, the affected target repeats the save, ending the spell on itself on a success.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. When you cast this spell with a spell slot of 5th level or higher, the initial damage of the spell increases by 1d10 for each spell level above 4.

docs.title: 1st-level Evocation Spell (Wizard)
docs.text:
Casting Time: Bonus Action, which you take immediately after hitting a target with a melee weapon or an Unarmed Strike

Range: Self

Component: V

Duration: 1 minute

As you hit the target, you teach an ally a short fact or proverb. The target takes add extra 1d8 radiant damage. Until the spell ends, the ally you taught can add 1d8 to the damage they deal with an attack or spell. The damage type is the same as the attack or spell that it is added to. Once the d8 is used, the spell ends.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. When you cast this spell with a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the number of allies you can teach increases by 1 for each slot level above 1st.

docs.title: 3rd-level Necromancy Spell (Necromancer, Wizard)
docs.text:
Casting Time: Action

Range: 150 feet

Component: V, S, M (a small vial of putrid methane gas or a piece of rotting flesh)

Duration: Instantaneous

You send a concentrated burst of necrotic energy toward a corpse or undead creature you can see within range, causing it to unleash a devastating explosion.

All creatures within a 10 foot Emmination of the target (including the target) must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw as the target explodes, taking 6d8 Force damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. If the original target was a corpse or if it is reduced to 0 hit points by this damage, it and everything non magical it is wearing and carrying are disintegrated into gray dust.

Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot. For each spell slot level above 3, the Force damage increases by 1d8 and the radius of the Emmination increases by 5 feet.

docs.title: Level 3: Adamantine Drill
docs.text:
When you finish a Long rest, you can use your Tinker’s Tools or Mason’s Tools to create an adamantine tipped drill in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of yourself. This drill is large enough to dig tunnels that you can travel through. The drill has the following traits.

Weapon Category: Simple Melee

Damage on a Hit: 1d8 Slashing plus the ability modifier used for the attack roll

Properties: Two-handed

Mastery: Sap (you can use this property, and it doesn’t count against the number of properties you can use with Weapon Mastery)

While holding your drill you gain the following benefits.

Enhanced Attacks. You can use your Intelligence modifier instead of your Strength modifier for the attack and damage rolls of your Adamantine Drill.

Adamantine Drill Bit. Whenever the Adamantine Drill hits an object, the hit is a Critical Hit.

Spellcasting Focus. You can use the Adamantine Drill as a Spellcasting Focus for your Artificer spells.

You can have only one drill at a time and can’t create one while you already have one.

docs.title: Level 3: Tunneling
docs.text:
While holding your drill you can use the following abilities.

Burrow. As a Magic Action, you can use your drill to tunnel under the ground. Until the end of your next turn, you gain a Burrow speed equal to your Speed and you gain Tremorsense with a range of 30 feet. You can burrow through nonmagical terrain, leaving a tunnel wide enough for a Medium sized creature to fit through.

Surface. While Burrowing, you can use your Bonus Action to rise to the surface, if you are no more than 10 feet below the surface. You must surface in an unoccupied space. If you surface within 5 feet of another creature, you can make one attack against that creature as part of the same Bonus action.

docs.title: Level 5: Extra Attack
docs.text: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. You can forgo one of your attacks when you take the Attack action to use your Burrow ability.

docs.title: Level 9: Dynamite
docs.text: When you use your Surface ability you may cause a small explosion as you emerge from the ground. When you do so each creature within a 10 foot Emanation of you makes a Dexterity saving throw against your Spell Save DC, taking 3d6 Fire damage on a failed save, or half as much on a success. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

docs.title: Path of the Dragon
docs.text: Ever felt the same fury that a dragon feels when an intruder dares step upon its horde? This fury is a daily feeling for Path of the Dragon Barbarians. Their rage is deeply tied to the primal draconic forces. By unleashing their fury, they unleash the power of the dragons themselves. Flying, breathing fire, and growing scales are just a few aspects of this transformation. These barbarians embody dragons in both body and spirit, feeling their fury and their power.

docs.title: Level 3: Chromatic Strike
docs.text: While your Rage is active, you can deal additional damage on each of your weapon attacks that use Strength. The extra damage equals 1d8, and its damage type is Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Poison (choose when you activate Rage).

docs.title: Level 6: Furious Breath
docs.text: When you activate your Rage, and as a Bonus Action on each turn while it is active, you can unleash a breath attack in a 15-foot Cone. Each creature in this cone must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Constitution modifier and Proficiency Bonus), taking damage equal to a number of d6s equal to your Rage Damage bonus. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage. The damage type for this feature is the same as the one you chose for Chromatic Strike.

docs.title: Level 10: Hardened Scales
docs.text: You grow hardened scales, which enhances your Unarmored Defense. While not wearing armor, your base AC equals 13 plus your Dexterity and Constitution Modifiers. You can use a Shield and still gain this benefit.

docs.title: Level 14: Draconic Presence
docs.text:
When you enter your Rage you gain the following benefits.

Soar. Spectral wings sprout from your back, granting you a Fly Speed equal to your Speed.

Roar. When you enter your Rage, you unleash a terrifying roar. Each creature of your choice within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 plus your Constitution modifier and Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, a target has the Frightened condition for 1 minute (a target can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success).

Gore. Your Chromatic strikes now deal an additional 2d8 damage of the chosen damage type (instead of 1d8).

Bard

docs.title: College of Law
docs.text: Many bards express their art through song, dance, and even swordsmanship. Not those that graduate from the College of Law, however. College of Law bards use their words like a fighter would use his shield and sword. These bards weave legal terms, magical enchantments, and devastating arguments like a master seamstress weaves a fine silk dress. They thrive in contract negotiations, settlement deals, and lawsuits. Any time a conflict can be resolved with a contract and a quill is a good day for a College of Law bard.

docs.title: Level 3: Legal Jargon
docs.text: You can lash out at foes, spouting legal jargon until their head spins. As a Bonus Action, you can expend a use of Bardic Inspiration, rolling a Bardic Inspiration die. When you do so, choose one creature that can hear you within 60 feet of you. The target makes an Intelligence saving throw against your Spell Save DC. On a failed save the target takes Psychic damage equal to the number rolled on the Bardic Inspiration die, and it has the Incapacitated condition until the end of its next turn.

docs.title: Level 3: Book of Contracts
docs.text: You gain a blank book, ready to be filled with all sorts of legal and magical contracts. You can scribe a contract into the book with any number of terms and conditions as you see fit. For each contract in your book, a number of willing creatures equal to your Charisma modifier can sign their name on a specific contract. When they do so, they are magically bound by the terms of the contract and are entitled to any benefits that it lists, that any of the other creatures bound by the contract are able to provide. Once the contract is signed by at least one creature, its writing can’t be changed by anything short of a Wish spell. Any creature that violates the terms of the contract must make a Wisdom saving throw against your Spell Save DC. On a failed save, the target takes psychic damage equal to 5 times your Bard level and you know its location until it remedies the violation or until it dies.

docs.title: Level 6: Objection
docs.text: You always have the spell Counterspell prepared and can cast it once without using a spell slot. When you cast this spell, you can expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration, rolling a Bardic Inspiration die.  When you do so, the target has a penalty to their Constitution saving throw equal to the number rolled on the Bardic Inspiration die.

docs.title: Level 14: Class Action Lawsuit
docs.text:
When a creature you can see deals damage with an attack, you can rally your allies to aid in their attack. Expend one use of your Bardic Inspiration and choose a number of willing creatures equal to your Charisma modifier (which can include yourself). Each creature can choose to spend their Reaction to add damage to the original attack. The original attack gains bonus Psychic damage equal to 1d12 for each creature that spent their Reaction.

Cleric

docs.title: Luck Domain
docs.text:
Luck always has two sides, resulting in repercussions that can help or hurt. While fortune may not always favor them, Luck Domain clerics are always willing to take risks to gain even the smallest benefit. They have experienced the glorious chaos of mortal life and understand that risks and rewards shape their fate. As a result, clerics who dedicate their lives to the gods of luck are often gamblers, charlatans, and performers. Driven by their own experiences with fate, these clerics use their relationship with luck to aid those in a downward spiral and to turn the tides on mortals that use their fortune unfavorably.

A Luck Domain cleric’s trust in their deity leads to them to be the ultimate wild cards, as they often rely on a roll of the dice or the flip of a coin. Whether one is on a losing or winning streak, everyone fears the uncertainty these clerics bring to the table. Yet regardless of their reputation, a Luck Domain cleric understands that while the house always wins, it is their job to make sure the 'house' is on the side of the righteous.

docs.title: Level 3: Discard Misfortune
docs.text: When a creature within 30 feet of you rolls a 1 on a D20 Test, you can use your Reaction to allow that creature to reroll the die, and it must use the new roll. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

docs.title: Level 3: Luck Domain Spells
docs.text:
Your connection to this divine domain ensures you always have certain spells ready. When you reach a Cleric level specified in the Luck Domain Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

Cleric Level Prepared Spells 3 Bane, Bless, Elminster’s Elusion, Magic Weapon 5 Beacon of Hope, Blink 7 Backlash, Confusion 9 Contact Other Plane, Reincarnate

docs.title: Level 3: Roll the Dice
docs.text:
As a Magic action, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity to manifest a boon or bane of pure chance. Roll a d6 to determine the effect from the table below.

1d6 1 Snake Eye. Each creature of your choice within 30 feet of you must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes 1d6 Poison damage and has the Poisoned condition until the end of its next turn. 2 Godspeed. Each creature of your choice within 30 feet of you has their Speed increased by 10 feet for 1 minute. 3 Bad Fortune. Each creature of your choice within 10 feet must make a Charisma saving throw or suffer the effects of the Bane spell for 1 minute. 4 Good Fortune. Each creature of your choice within 10 feet of you gains the benefits of the Bless spell for 1 minute. 5 Lucky Break. Each creature of your choice within 15 feet of you regains Hit Points equal to 1d6 + your Wisdom modifier. 6 Boxcar. An ethereal box car runs along a 5 foot wide, 30 foot long line originating at a point you choose within 60 feet of you. Each creature in the area must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes 2d6 Force damage and falls Prone. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage and does not fall prone.

docs.title: Level 6: Life’s a Gamble
docs.text: When you drop to 0 hit points, you can choose to make a single death saving throw to determine your fate. On a success, roll a number of d4s equal to your Cleric Level and regain that many Hit Points. On a failure, you suffer two death saving throw failures. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

docs.title: Level 17: The House Always Wins
docs.text:
As a Bonus Action, you can enter a state of heightened awareness and control for 1 minute. You see the golden threads of fate as they weave around you and you can bend them to your will. When you use this feature, you can designate any number of creatures that you can see within 30 feet of you (including yourself) to gain the following benefits.

Beat the Odds. When the creature fails a Saving Throw, it can choose to succeed instead. A creature can only use this benefit once per use of this ability.

Double Down. When the creature lands a Critical Hit with an Attack roll, it deals additional 4d6 damage.

House Edge. Whenever the creature rolls a D20 Test, they can treat any roll of 7 or lower as an 8 on the die.

Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 6+ spell slot (no action required).

docs.title: Pestilence Domain
docs.text: Clerics who pray to gods of pestilence and disease are extraordinarily uncommon. Most clerics dedicate years to the study of purifying food, curing diseases, and preventing death. Pestilence domain clerics, on the other hand, believe that decay and rot are a necessary step in the natural cycle of life. They live to spread glorious plague throughout the land. Rotting crops, poisoning water, and spreading disease are all necessary steps in order to cleanse the earth of the weak and for the next cycle to begin. Sure, many will succumb to illness, but that is a small price to pay for the sweet stench of plague ridden corpses.

docs.title: Level 3: Leach
docs.text:
Once per turn, whenever you deal damage to a creature that has the Poisoned condition with an attack or a Cleric spell, you can choose to deal an additional 2d6 Necrotic damage. When you do so, you regain a number of hitpoints equal to the Necrotic damage dealt by this feature.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once) and regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

docs.title: Level 3: Pestilence Domain Spells
docs.text:
Your connection to this divine domain ensures you always have certain spells ready. When you reach a Cleric level specified in the Pestilence Domain Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

Cleric Level Prepared Spells 3 Inflict Wounds, Ray of Sickness, Ray of Enfeeblement, Web 5 Stinking Cloud, Vampiric Touch 7 Blight, Giant Insect 9 Contagion, Insect Plague

docs.title: Level 3: Supernatural Decay
docs.text: As a Magic action, you present your Holy Symbol and expend a use of your Channel Divinity to emit an aura of decay in a 10-foot Emanation originating from yourself for 1 minute. Any creatures that enter the area for the first time, or start their turn in it must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save the target takes 3d8 Poison damage and has the Poisoned condition. On a successful save, a target takes half as much damage, isn't Poisoned, and is immune to this effect for 24 hours.

docs.title: Level 6: Improved Leach
docs.text:
You regain all expended uses of your Leach when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

You can now activate Leach whenever you deal damage with a melee weapon or a spell that deals Poison or Necrotic damage, even if the target doesn’t have the Poisoned condition.

docs.title: Level 17: Pandemic
docs.text:
Whenever you cast a spell with a casting time of one Action that targets one creature and deals Poison damage, Necrotic damage, or inflicts the Poisoned condition, you can target another creature with that spell as part of the same Action, given that the second target is also in the spell’s range.

Monk

docs.title: Warrior of the Mage Slayer
docs.text: Many monks use mana and magic as a byproduct of their Ki mastery. Many go their whole lives without realizing that their Ki is even connected to the weave at all. Mage Slayer monks are the exception. They use their Ki to grab hold of the weave; bending it, shaping it, and blocking it. They flow magic through their body to enhance their martial arts and Ki capabilities. These Monks feel a very visceral connection to the weave that few others ever experience. Magic becomes a part of them and they become a part of it, uniting their souls with the weave. Due to their physical prowess and unmatched control over the flow of magic, they are often called in when a crazed sorcerer or mad wizard has amassed too much power to be taken out by conventional means.

docs.title: Level 3: Mage Slayer’s Mark
docs.text:
Once per turn when you hit a creature with a Monk weapon or an Unarmed Strike, you can expend 1 Focus Point to mark the target you hit. The mark lasts for 1 minute or until you use this feature to mark a second target. The mark confers the following benefits for the duration.

Glass Canon. The marked target must subtract 1d4 from every Constitution saving throw it makes.

Beat Down. Your attacks with Monk weapons and Unarmed Strikes deal additional damage equal to your Wisdom modifier to the marked target.

No Hiding. You are aware of the target’s location at all times and can see it even when it has the Invisible condition.

docs.title: Level 6: Improved Mark
docs.text:
You have improved your focus and increased the capabilities of your Mage Slayer’s Mark. Your mark now confers the following for the duration.

Weave Guide. You add 1d4 to the attack rolls you make Monk weapons or Unarmed Strikes against targets marked by Mage Slayer’s Mark.

Sapping Speed. While marked, the target’s Speed is reduced by 10 feet.

docs.title: Level 11: Arcane Interruption
docs.text: You learn to resist the flow of magic with your Ki. You can spend 3 Focus Points to cast Counterspell  or Dispel Magic as a 3rd-level spell. You can increase either spell’s level by 1 for each additional Focus Point you spend, up to a number of Focus Points equal to half of your level, rounded down. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

docs.title: Level 17: Weavebreaker
docs.text:
Your gaze can nullify magical effects for targets you have marked. As a Bonus Action, you can spend 6 Focus Points to prevent a creature you have marked with Mage Slayer’s Mark from using magic entirely. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw or be under the following effects for 1 minute, or until you lose your Concentration (as if you were concentrating on a spell).

Antimagic. The target and everything it is wearing or carrying is under the effects of an Antimagic Field.

Spellblocked. The target cannot cast spells or take the Magic Action.

Shatter Concentration. The target loses Concentration on any spell it is currently concentrating on.

docs.title: (Too scared to delete, use for another subclass) Level 6: Arcane Flow
docs.text:
You can infuse arcane power into your Ki abilities. When you roll Initiative or at the start of your turn, you can enter a state of magical synergy. You can maintain this state for up to 1 minute. While in this state you gain the following options.

Eldritch Fists. When you use Flurry of Blows, you can imbue your fists with arcane energy. You add 1d4 to the damage rolls you make as part of Flurry of Blows.

Retaliating Defense. When you use Patient Defense you weave magic to further protect yourself. After you use Patient Defense you gain a +2 bonus to AC until the start of your next turn.

Arcane Propulsion. When you use Step of the Wind, you blast off with an arcane explosion. All creatures of your choice within 5 feet of you must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, a creature takes Force damage equal to one roll of your Martial Arts Die plus your Wisdom modifier.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom Modifier (minimum of once) , and regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

Paladin

docs.title: Oath of the Sunlight Guardian
docs.text: Paladins that take upon the Oath of the Sunlight Guardian swear to protect the innocent and bring light to the darkness. These paladins have a deep connection to gods of light, sunshine, and protection. Often, sunlight guardians will favor tactics that save their allies over damaging their foes. While burning the evil with holy light is a necessary job of any paladin, Sunlight Guardians tend to favor shielding the innocent than punishing the wicked.

docs.title: Level 3: Oath of the Sunlight Guardian Spells
docs.text: Paladin Level Prepared Spells 3 Faerie Fire, Sanctuary 5 Shining Smite, Warding Bond 9 Blinding Smite, Daylight 13 Fire Shield, Guardian of Faith 17 Dispel Evil and Good, Summon Celestial

docs.title: Level 3: Radiant Shell
docs.text: As a Magic action on your turn, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity to shed Bright Light in a 10-foot Emanation around you for 1 minute. Each creature of your choice in the area gains a bonus to AC equal to half your Proficiency Bonus (rounded down).

docs.title: Level 7: Sunlight Sacrifice
docs.text: Once per turn, when you deal Radiant damage to a creature with a weapon attack or a Spell, you can forgo dealing any Radiant damage, instead granting Temporary hit points to each creature within your aura of protection (including yourself). The number of Temporary hit points is equal to the amount of Radiant damage you would have dealt.

docs.title: Level 15: Solar Protection
docs.text: When a creature within your Aura of Protection is hit with an attack roll, you can take a Reaction to halve the attack's damage against the creature.

docs.title: Level 20: Sunbringer
docs.text:
As a Bonus Action, you can embody the sun itself for 1 minute, empowering your Aura of Protection. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 5 spell slot (no action required).

Protector. Attacks against creatures of your choice in the aura have Disadvantage.

Radiance. Creatures of your choice in the aura can deal an extra 1d8 Radiant damage on attacks with weapons and Unarmed Strikes.

Sunlight. The aura is filled with Bright Light that is Sunlight.

docs.title: Field Medic
docs.text: Many Rogues use their dexterity, skill, and bladework to steal, kill, and spy. Field Medics take another path. They focus on honing their medical practice, improving their ability to quickly apply bandages, administer medicine, and stitch wounds. Their roguish skill makes them excellent battlefield healers, even if they don’t have access to potent healing magic. Field Medics are adaptable and always ready to apply an antidote to an ally or cut a foe’s vital artery.

docs.title: Level 3: The Doctor Is In
docs.text: You gain a healer’s kit and gain Proficiency in Medicine. If you are already proficient in medicine, you gain Expertise in Medicine. If you already have Expertise in Medicine, you gain proficiency in a different skill of your choice.

docs.title: Level 3: First Aid
docs.text:
You can use a Bonus Action to do the following.

Triage. Take the Help action to stabilize a creature or take the Utilize action to use a Healer’s Kit.

Fast Acting Medicine. You can patch up your wounds or the wounds of another creature within 5 feet of you. The creature can roll up to half of their Hit Dice, adding their Constitution modifier to each dice rolled. They regain hit points equal to the total of the dice and modifiers. A creature can only benefit from this feature once, and can do so again after finishing a Long Rest.

docs.title: Level 9: Improvised Antidotes
docs.text: Whenever you use your Fast Acting Medicine ability, you can remove one of the following conditions from the creature you heal: Blinded, Deafened, Paralyzed, or Poisoned.

docs.title: Level 13: Potent Healing
docs.text: You have improved your ability to mend other’s wounds. Whenever you use Fast Acting medicine, the creature you heal regains the maximum number of hitpoints possible for all Hit Dice rolls.

docs.title: Level 17: Plague Doctor
docs.text:
You gain the following Cunning Strike options.

Lobotomy (Cost: 4d6). You strike the through target’s skull, piercing its brain. The target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save the target has the Stunned condition until the start of your next turn.

Bloodletting (Cost: 2d6). You cut a vital artery or infect your target with leeches, forcing the target to make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the target gains 1 level of Exhaustion.

Sorcerer

docs.title: Serpent Sorcery
docs.text: Serpan sorcery is an ancient bloodline of enchantments, poisons, and constriction. Many who possess serpent sorcery descend from medusa, yuan-ti, or ancient snake gods. Oftentimes those who develop these powers end up as spies, assassins, and infiltrators. Serpent sorcery may not be the most glamorous source of mystical power, but it certainly gets the job done. A dragon sorcerer might level a town with blasts of fire and ice, but a serpent sorcerer will topple a kingdom with just a few well placed toxins and enchantments.

docs.title: Level 3: Serpent Spells
docs.text:
When you reach a Sorcerer level specified in the Serpent Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

Sorcerer Level Prepared Spells 3 Charm Person, Ray of Sickness, Suggestion, Summon Beast 5 Syluné’s Viper, Hypnotic Pattern 7 Charm Monster, Grasping Vine 9 Cloudkill, Geas

docs.title: Level 3: Snake Charm
docs.text: When you charm a creature with a level 1+ spell, that charm can’t be broken as a result of you dealing Poison damage to that creature.

docs.title: Level 6: Venomous
docs.text: Whenever you Poison damage with a spell, you can add your Charisma modifier to one damage roll of that spell. Additionally, you have resistance to Poison damage and have Advantage on saving throws made to avoid or end the Poisoned condition.

docs.title: Level 14: Serpent Form
docs.text: You can cast Polymorph without a spell slot, targeting yourself and selecting one of the following options: Giant Constrictor Snake, Giant Venomous Snake, or Flying Snake. You can use this feature twice and regain the ability to do so when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

docs.title: Level 18: Medusa
docs.text:
You can cast Flesh to Stone without using a spell slot. When you do so, the target has Disadvantage on saves made to avoid the spell’s effects. Once you use this feature you can’t do so again until you finish a Long Rest. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 6 spell slot (no action required).

Warlock

docs.title: Level 3: Belittle
docs.text: When you cast Vicious Mockery, if the target misses the next attack it makes before the end of its next turn, you can use your Reaction to cast Vicious Mockery again at the creature.

docs.title: Level 3: Trickster Spells
docs.text: Warlock Level Spells 3 Charm Person, Invisibility, Phantasmal Force, Tasha’s Hideous Laughter, Vicious Mockery 5 Hypnotic Pattern, Major Image 7 Greater Invisibility, Confusion 9 Dream, Modify Memory

docs.title: Level 6: Trickster’s Escape
docs.text: When you are hit by an attack, you can take a Reaction to teleport to an unoccupied space within 30 feet of you, and you gain the Invisible condition for 1 minute, or until you attack or cast a spell. You can use this feature once and regain the ability to do so when you finish a Short Rest.

docs.title: Level 10: Convincing Illusions
docs.text: When a creature takes the Study action to determine if an illusion that you created is real, they have Disadvantage on their Intelligence (Investigation) check. Additionally, while a creature perceives one of your illusions, you gain Advantage on Charisma checks against that creature.

docs.title: Level 14: Subtlety
docs.text:
When you cast a spell while you have the Invisible condition, targets of that spell have Disadvantage on any saving throws made to avoid the spell.

Wizard

docs.title: Pugilist
docs.text: Tired of cowardly backline wizards? Wish you could just punch that orc with a little bit more juice? Look no further than the Pugilist. Pugilist wizards are a far cry different from the average spell chucker and book worm. Sure they study and learn magic just like a normal wizard would, but a pugilist believes that a sharp mind requires one to also sharpen the body. Pugilists use their magic to enhance their punching, weaving, and brawling capabilities. After all, it takes a real wizard to test their magical abilities head on against a stronger opponent.

docs.title: Level 3: Pugilist’s Armor
docs.text:
You can cast the Mage Armor spell on yourself without expending a spell slot. When you cast Mage Armor in this way, you can instead set your AC equal to 10 + your Intelligence modifier + your Dexterity modifier.

At level 14, your AC while using Mage Armor in this way increases to 13 + your Intelligence modifier + your Dexterity modifier

docs.title: Level 3: Arcane Fist
docs.text:
When you deal damage with a spell that requires a melee spell attack, you can deal additional damage equal to your Intelligence Modifier.

Additionally, when you cast a spell that requires a ranged spell attack, you can choose to reduce the range of the spell to touch and make a melee spell attack instead.

docs.title: Level 6: Punch and Weave
docs.text: Once on your turn, when you hit a creature with a melee spell attack, you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Intelligence Modifier and your movement doesn’t provoke opportunity attacks until the end of your turn.

docs.title: Level 10: Jab Cross
docs.text: When you cast a spell with a casting time of an action, you can use your Bonus Action to cast a Cantrip that requires a melee or ranged spell attack. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier and regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

docs.title: Level 14: Knock Out
docs.text:
When a creature within 5 feet of you makes an attack or casts a spell, you can use your Reaction to expend a spell slot of level 3 or higher. When you do so, make a melee spell attack against the creature. If the attack lands, the target takes Force damage equal to 3d8 + your Intelligence modifier and must make a Constitution saving throw vs your spell save DC. On a failed save, the target has the Incapacitated condition until the end of their turn. This attack happens before the initiating attack or spell takes effect, interrupting the attack or spell if the target fails its save.

docs.title: Level 1: Show Weapon
docs.text:
You have specialized in performing with a particular type of weapon. Choose one type of melee weapon to designate as your Show Weapon. You can use hands holding weapons designated as your Show Weapon to grapple and shove as if they were free.

Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can practice with another weapon to change the kind of weapon you designate as your Show Weapon.

Some features that use your Show Weapon or Unarmed Strikes require your target to make a saving throw. The save DC equals 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and Proficiency Bonus.

docs.title: Level 1: Unarmored Defense
docs.text: While you aren’t wearing armor or wielding a Shield, your base Armor Class equals 10 plus your Strength and Dexterity Modifiers.

docs.title: Level 1: Weapon Mastery
docs.text:
Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of two kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency, such as Handaxes and Mauls.

Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose. For example, you could switch to using the mastery properties of Scimitars and Pikes.

docs.title: Level 2: Fighting Style
docs.text:
You gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice (see chapter 5).

Whenever you gain an Acrobat level, you can replace the feat you chose with a different Fighting Style feat.

docs.title: Level 2: Gymnastics
docs.text:
You have trained in moving your body in ways that seem impossible to others.

Glorious Vault. As a Bonus action while you’re standing, you can spend 10 feet of movement to jump a number of feet equal to 5 times your Strength modifier to a point you can reach within range. If the point you end your jump at is in the air, you fall directly downwards to the ground. You do not need to move any distance before making this jump.

Elegant Rebound. When you have the Prone condition, you can right yourself with only 5 feet of movement.

Masterful Climbing. You gain a Climb Speed equal to your Speed.

docs.title: Level 3: Acrobat Subclass
docs.text: You gain an Acrobat subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Acrobat levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass’s features that are of your Acrobat level or lower.

docs.title: Level 3: Expertise
docs.text:
You gain Expertise in two of your skill proficiencies of your choice. Athletics and Performance are recommended if you have proficiency in them.

At Acrobat level 7, you gain Expertise in two more skill proficiencies of your choice.

docs.title: Level 4: Ability Score Increase
docs.text: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Acrobat levels 8, 10, 12, and 16.

docs.title: Level 4: Graceful Tumbling
docs.text: When you take damage from falling, you only take half of the damage you would normally take. Additionally, you can choose to land on your feet instead of falling prone when you land.

docs.title: Level 5: Arrogant Display
docs.text:
Your shows have grown grander, and you won’t fail to astound. As a Bonus action, you may enter your Arrogant Display for a number of rounds equal to your Performance modifier or until you become Incapacitated. Now and at the start of each of your turns while your Arrogant Display is active, you may choose to decrease your armor class by 1 until the start of your next turn. If you do, attacks made with your Show Weapon and unarmed strikes add both your Dexterity and Strength modifiers to their damage rolls until the end of your current turn. Additionally, while your Arrogant Display is active, your movement speed increases by a number of feet equal to 5 times your Proficiency Bonus.

You can enter your Arrogant Display the number of times shown for your Acrobat level in the Arrogant Display column of the Barbarian Features table. You regain all expended uses when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

docs.title: Level 5: Extra Attack
docs.text: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

docs.title: Level 6: Brawling
docs.text:
Once per turn, when you hit a target with your Show Weapon or an Unarmed Strike, you can also perform one of the following actions with the same attack. If you use your Show Weapon in this way, perform the action as if you had performed an Unarmed Strike (see rules glossary).

Grapple. You attempt to grapple the target if they’re within 5 feet of you.

Shove. You attempt to shove the target.

Disarm. If your target is holding a weapon or another object (such as a spellcasting focus) you can attempt to disarm them of that item. Make a Strength (Athletics) check contested by the target’s Dexterity or Strength score (whichever is higher). If your check equals or exceeds their ability score, they drop the item they are holding.

Climb Enemy. If the enemy is at least one size larger than you, you can attempt to climb it. Make a Dexterity (Acrobatics) check contested by the target’s Strength score. If your roll equals or exceeds the target’s ability score you climb onto it. While climbing it, You have advantage on all attacks made against the creature you are climbing, cannot push or pull it, and are moved with it. The target can attempt to remove you at the end of each of its turns by making a Strength (Athletics) contested by your original Dexterity (Acrobatics) roll. If the target’s roll equals or exceeds your roll, you fall prone in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the target. If the target teleports, or you are moved out of the creature’s space, you stop climbing it and land prone in an unoccupied space.

docs.title: Level 7: Evasion
docs.text: You can nimbly dodge out of the way of certain dangers. When you're subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw and only half damage if you fail. You can't use this feature if you have the Incapacitated condition.

docs.title: Level 8: Bounding Leaps
docs.text: Whenever you use Glorious Vault, the maximum distance that you can jump is increased by a number of feet equal to 5 times your Dexterity modifier.

docs.title: Level 9: Stage Falling
docs.text: You can use your Glorious Vault to slam into enemies. When you use your Glorious Vault and choose to end your jump in another creature’s space, you can attempt to topple them over as part of the same Bonus Action. The target must make a Strength or Dexterity saving throw (it choses) against your Show Weapon DC. On a failed save the target falls prone and takes bludgeoning damage equal to 1d10 + your Strength modifier/. After they fall prone, you land in an unoccupied space of your choice within 5 feet of the target. On a successful save, you fall prone in an unoccupied space of your choice within 5 feet of the target.

docs.title: Level 10: Escape Artist
docs.text:
You gain Thieves' tools, and you have proficiency with them. You also gain a Swim Speed equal to your Walking Speed.

Additionally, whenever you are grappled or restrained, on your turn you can spend 5 feet of movement to escape unless you are bound by magical restraints.

docs.title: Level 13: Greater Brawling
docs.text:
Some of the options in your Brawling ability gain the following benefits.

Grapple. The target of your grapple is also restrained until the grapple ends.

Shove. The distance you shove the target increases by 10 feet. Additionally, you can choose to move them and cause them to fall prone in the same attack. The creature rolls one save for both effects.

docs.title: Level 14: Grandiose Display
docs.text: When you use your Arrogant Display, and at the start of each of your turns while your Arrogant Display is active, when you decrease your Armor Class you may choose to decrease your armor class again by 1 until the end of your next turn. If you do, attacks made with your Show Weapon and unarmed strikes you deal this turn also deal an additional 1d10 damage. This additional damage is the same type as the Show weapon used.

docs.title: Level 17: Superior Brawling
docs.text:
You gain two more options that you can use when you use your Bawling ability.

Twirl. Once per turn, when you hit a target with your Show Weapon or an Unarmed Strike, you can make another attack against a different creature within your reach. Use the same attack roll against the second target, if the attack hits, use the same damage roll that you used for the first target.

Spin. Once per turn, when you hit a target with your Show Weapon or an Unarmed Strike, you can cause the target to spin uncontrollably. The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or have the incapacitated condition until the end of its next turn.

docs.title: Level 18: Defy Gravity
docs.text: You are immune to damage from falling.

docs.title: Level 19: Epic Boon
docs.text: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Fate is recommended.

docs.title: Level 20: Greatest Showman
docs.text:
You have honed your muscles to even greater heights. Your Strength and Dexterity scores increase by 2, to a maximum of 23.

Additionally, when you roll initiative, you may automatically enter your Arrogant Display without needing to spend a Bonus Action to do so.

docs.title: Level 3: The Best Medicine
docs.text:
When you hit a target with a Show Weapon that you are wielding in two hands, you can cast Tasha’s Hideous Laughter without using a spell slot as a Bonus action, targeting the creature that you hit with your weapon. The spell save DC for this spell is your Show Weapon DC when you cast this spell in this way. The Show Weapon must have the Two-Handed or Versatile property to gain this benefit.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus. You regain all expended uses after completing a Long Rest.

docs.title: Level 6: Sinister Smile
docs.text:
If you perform for at least 1 minute, you can attempt to seed paranoia and fear into the minds of up to five humanoids who can hear your performance. At the end of the performance, make a Charisma (Intimidation) check and the targets must each make a Wisdom (Insight) check. If your roll equals or exceeds the target’s, it is Frightened of you for 1 hour.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short Rest or Long Rest.

docs.title: Level 11: Unnerving Smash
docs.text: Attacks you make with a Show Weapon that you are wielding in two hands deal an additional 1d8 psychic damage. Additionally, once per turn when you deal psychic damage, you can strike terror into your target, forcing it to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the target is frightened of you until the start of your next turn. The extra damage from this ability is considered part of the weapon’s damage dice.

docs.title: Level 15: Feed on Fear
docs.text:
You can now use the terror you inflict to sustain and empower yourself. At the start of your turn while your Arrogant Display is active you gain one of the following benefits, choosing at the start of each turn. Each option increases in power for each creature that is frightened of you or under the effect of Tasha’s Hideous Laughter, hereafter called your “captive audience”.

Scared to Death. Your Show Weapon attacks deal an extra 1d8 psychic damage for each captive audience member until the end of your current turn.

The Show Must Go On. You regain 1d8 Hit Points for each captive audience member.

Big Red Shoes. Your walking speed increases by 5 feet for each captive audience member.

docs.title: Level 3: Fire Dance
docs.text: You have the Produce Flame and Elementalism chantrips prepared and can cast them without material components. When you cast Elementalism in this way, you can only control fire. Your spellcasting ability for these spells is Dexterity.

docs.title: Level 6: Flame’s Touch
docs.text:
While your Arrogant Display is active, attacks you make with a Show Weapon that has the Finesse property to deal an additional 1d6 fire damage. Additionally, when you take the attack action in your turn, you can cast Produce Flame in place of one of the attacks you make with that action.

The additional damage dealt this way increases to 2d6 at level 15.

docs.title: Level 11: Heat Wave
docs.text:
You can cast Fireball or Wall of Fire as a 4th-level spell without spending a spell slot, using your Show Weapon DC. You can use this feature twice, and regain all expended uses on a long rest.

Additionally you have Resistance to fire damage, Immunity to fire damage dealt by your Firebreather abilities, and your Firebreather abilities ignore Resistance to fire damage.

docs.title: Level 15: Blinding Display
docs.text: When you activate your Arrogant Display all creatures of your choice within 15 feet of you must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 4d10 fire damage and has the Blinded condition for 1 minute. Creatures blinded in this way can repeat this save at the end of each of their turns, ending the effect on a success. On a successful save, a creature takes half damage only.

docs.title: Level 3: Combat Juggling
docs.text: When you roll Initiative, you can immediately draw up to 5 Show Weapons with the Thrown property and begin to juggle. Any Show Weapons that you are juggling will ricochet back to your hands after being thrown at a target (even if the attack misses).

docs.title: Level 6: Blade Waltz
docs.text:
Your juggling skills have gone beyond the mundane, allowing you to cause knives to juggle themselves. When you hit a creature with a thrown attack using a Show Weapon, you can immediately cast Cloud of Daggers without spending a spell slot, centered on the creature you hit, and your concentration can’t be broken as a result of taking damage.

You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus and regain all expended uses on a Long Rest.

docs.title: Level 11: Go For The Juggler
docs.text:
While your Arrogant Display is active, you can draw or stow an additional two weapons on each of your turns, and can juggle up to 10 Show Weapons at once.

Additionally while your Arrogant Display is active, you can perform an Attack action, spending all attacks to throw all weapons you are currently juggling, making an attack for each weapon against targets within range. When you do, weapons do not benefit from Combat Juggling.

docs.title: Level 15: Colossus Juggler
docs.text: While your Arrogant Display is active, you enter a state of extreme focus and strength. During this time, you’re considered one size larger for effects such as grappling, carrying capacity, and throwing. Additionally, you can throw a creature you are grappling if it is your size or smaller. You can throw a creature a number of feet equal to 5 times your proficiency modifier. When you do, treat the creature you throw as a weapon with the thrown property that deals 1d6 damage to the creature if it’s Small or smaller, 2d6 if it's Medium, or 3d6 if it's Large or larger. On a hit against another creature, both the thrown creature and the target take the damage dealt this way.

docs.title: Level 3: Three Ring Circus
docs.text:
Once per turn, when you attack using your Show Weapon, you may target an additional creature within reach of your weapon.

You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency modifier and regain all expended uses on a long rest.

docs.title: Level 6: Beast Tamer
docs.text: You can now quickly call upon a trained animal to aid in your act. You can cast Summon Beast as a 2nd-level spell without spending a spell slot, using Dexterity as the spell casting ability. You can use this feature twice, and regain all expended uses on a long rest.

docs.title: Level 11: Tandem Takedown
docs.text:
Creatures have Disadvantage on saving throws made to resist or end your Brawling ability as long as they are adjacent to one or more of your allies.

Additionally, you can attempt to grapple creatures if they’re up to 10 feet away from you and within reach of your Show Weapon.

docs.title: Level 15: Whip Cracking
docs.text: While your Arrogant Display is active, attacks you make with a Show Weapon against a creature exactly 10 feet away from you deal an additional 2d10 damage of the weapon’s damage type.

docs.title: Arbiter
docs.text:
Arbiter

A half-orc clad in plate armor uses his maul to land a devastating blow against the ogre. He quickly shifts into a defensive stance, his weapons flash a bright white light. Suddenly he is holding a longsword and shield, ready to deflect the ogre’s attacks to protect his allies.

A tiefling wearing studded leather armor draws her bow back and shoots an arrow through the gaps in a warlord’s armor. As soon as the arrow leaves her bow, she breaks into a sprint, charging at the warlord. As the arrow hits the warlord, she plunges a dagger through his chest, swiftly behind the arrow as if performed in a single stroke.

A dragonborn armored in scale mail slices off one of a beholder’s eyestalks with a flaming sword. Before the beholder gets a chance to respond, a bolt of lightning, fired from the dragonborn’s crossbow, strikes its central eye, closing it forever.

No matter what form an Arbiter takes, they use their ability to switch between tactics and weapons to surprise their foes and adapt to a chaotic battlefield. While others might struggle to readjust quickly, Arbiters thrive in an unrelenting and unpredictable fight.

docs.title: Versatile Champions
docs.text: Most warriors spend their days honing their expertise in a single weapon, practicing the alignment of their sword’s edge, honing their fists into lethal weapons, or perfecting their aim with a longbow. Arbiters believe that a jack of all trades is often superior to a master of one, using their wide breadth of knowledge to give them an edge no matter what happens on the battlefield. Arbiters are trained in every type of armor and weapon available and are able to switch between weapons at a moment’s notice. Arbiters can even augment their armor to enhance their tactical prowess. An arbiter's armor augmentations are unique to their training, whether they descended from an ancient order of similar knights, or if they stumbled upon this power while exploring ancient tombs or ruins.

docs.title: Protectors of the Realms
docs.text:
The magic of requipping was discovered long ago by knights looking for a way to harness the power of extradimensional spaces. Since then, these knights have taken on the responsibility of protecting the realms from evil within and without. They keep vast records of extraplanar forces and creatures. These orders are often small and kept secret from the majority of commoners in order to keep themselves safe.

Hailing from an ancient order isn't the only way to become an Arbiter. Many arbiters discover their power through experimentation with bags of holding or similar magical items. Some discover the power by happenstance while spelunking in ancient ruins or reading dusty old tombs.

docs.title: Creating an Arbiter
docs.text:
As you build your Arbiter, think about how you discovered this power: Were you knight descended from an ancient order of protectors? Were you the product of magical experimentation by a powerful wizard? Was this power passed down to you through your bloodline or from a wise older tutor? What drove you to learn and master this power? A sense of duty, a code of honor, or just a rabid curiosity could all be reasons for developing your skills as an arbiter.

What drew you to the adventuring lifestyle? Were you sent on a wild goose chase by a wealthy patron? Did your order task you to go out and protect the innocent? Are you seeking to avenge the death of a loved one or mentor who was taken away by a powerful foe? Consider how your character fits into the narrative and talk with your DM about how you might have learned this power.

A Half-Elf discovers the magic or Requiping while escaping a dungeon

docs.title: Becoming an Arbiter…
docs.text:
As a 1st Level Character

  • Gain all the traits in the Core Arbiter Traits table.
  • Gain the Arbiter’s level 1 features, which are listed in the Arbiter Features Table.

As a Multiclass Character

  • Gain the following traits from the Core Arbiter Traits table: Hit Point Die, proficiency with Martial weapons, and training with Light and Medium armor and Shields.
  • Gain the Arbiter’s level 1 features, which are listed in the Arbiter Features table.

Weapon Proficiencies Simple and Martial weapons Tool Proficiencies Smith’s Tools Armor Training Light, Medium, Heavy armor and Shields Starting Equipment Choose A, B, or C: (A) Chain Mail, Longsword, Shield, 2 Javelins, Smith’s Tools, Dungeoneer’s Pack, and 17 GP; (B) Studded Leather Armor, Shortsword, Dagger, Longbow, 20 Arrows, Quiver,  Smith’s Tools, Dungeoneer’s Pack, and 9 GP; or (C) 150 GP
