docs.title: Level 1: Requip
docs.text:
When you take the Attack action on your turn, you can magically summon a Set of weapons into your hands. You can do this before each attack you make on your turn. Each time you summon a new Set of weapons, the former Set disappears back into an extradimensional space, called an Armory.

While you are holding a weapon summoned from your Armory, if the weapon leaves your hand, you can instantly return it to your hand at the end of your turn if you have a free hand to hold the weapon. If the weapon was thrown, it returns to your hand immediately after it hits or misses its target. You cannot be disarmed of any weapons or shields summoned from your Armory unless you have the  Incapacitated condition.

Your Arbiter level determines the number of Sets that you can store in your Armory at one time, as shown in the Weapon Sets column of the Arbiter table. A Set of weapons can contain any number of Simple weapons, Martial weapons or Shields that you can wield at one time. For example, you can have a one handed weapon and a Shield, two one handed weapons that have the Light property, or a two handed weapon in a single set.

You can change the weapons that are in your Armory at the end of a Short or Long Rest by touching a new Set and magically sending it into the Armory. If there are no free spaces in the Armory, doing so would replace one of the current sets, which would drop to the ground in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you.

When you die, your Armory ceases to exist and all weapons and Shields stored in it appear in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of your body.

docs.title: Level 1: Fighting Style
docs.text: You adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. You gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice. You gain this feature again at Arbiter levels 5, 9, 13, and 18.

docs.title: Level 1: Weapon Mastery
docs.text:
Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of three kinds of Simple or Martial weapons of your choice. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can practice weapon drills and change one of those weapon choices.

When you reach certain Arbiter  levels, you gain the ability to use the mastery properties of more kinds of weapons, as shown in the Weapon Mastery column of the Arbiter Features table.

docs.title: Level 2: Phase Step
docs.text: Once per turn, when you use your Requip feature, you can move up to 10 feet as part of your movement without provoking Opportunity Attacks. This movement occurs immediately before you make your first attack with the newly equipped weapon.

docs.title: Level 3: Knight’s Creed
docs.text: You choose a Knight's Creed that represents the order of arbiters that you hail from or the source of your magical power. Choose Armor of the Giant's Bulwark, Armor of the Dreadful Duelist, or Armor of the Elemental Emperor, all detailed at the end of the class description. Some of the features granted to you by your Knight’s Creed require a saving throw, The DC for these saving throws is 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Intelligence modifier. The Creed you choose grants you features at 3rd level and again at 6th, 9th, 15th, and 17th level.

docs.title: Level 4: Ability Score Improvement
docs.text: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Arbiter levels 8, 12, 14, and 16.

docs.title: Level 5: Extra Attack
docs.text: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

docs.title: Level 7: Improved Requip
docs.text: When you use your Requip feature you can also change which armor type is active.

docs.title: Level 7: Tactical Defense
docs.text: You can use your tactical wit to evade harmful effects. You can add a bonus to your saving throws equal to your Intelligence modifier (with a minimum bonus of +1). You cannot benefit from this feature while Incapacitated.

docs.title: Level 10: Planar Synergy
docs.text: Your Requip leaves behind dimensional traces that bolster the damage your weapons deal. After you Requip, your next weapon attack deals additional Force damage equal to your Intelligence modifier.

docs.title: Level 11: Dancing Weapon
docs.text:
You gain the ability to magically animate your weapons. As a Bonus Action, you can summon one of your Weapon Sets from your Armory to a space within 60 feet of you. When you do so, you can use the Dancing Weapon to make a weapon attack against one creature within the weapon’s range. The Dancing Weapon uses the same attack bonus and damage dice that it would have if you were to wield it. The Dancing Weapon benefits from any Fighting Style Feats, Class Features, or Feats that you have that can apply to the Dancing Weapon. 

The Weapon is animated for 1 minute, until you lose Concentration (as if you were concentrating on a spell). As a Bonus Action on your turn, you can move the Dancing Weapon up to 30 feet and repeat the attack against a creature within the weapon’s range. When this ability ends, the weapons instantly return to your Armory.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

docs.title: Level 18: Duet
docs.text: You can instantly warp yourself to your Dancing Weapon. If your Dancing Weapon is active and the weapon is within 60 feet of you, you can teleport to it. Once per turn, when you Requip, you teleport to the Dancing Weapon’s location and equip the Weapon Set that was animated. The Weapon Set you had equipped before teleporting now acts as your Dancing Weapon and stays in the space you occupied before teleporting until you command it to move.

docs.title: Level 19: Epic Boon
docs.text: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Irresistible Offense is recommended.

docs.title: Level 20: Planar Onslaught
docs.text: You Requip with uncanny speed and precision which causes your weapons to radiate destructive magic, bolstering your attacks. When you Requip, you can enter a state of heightened power. While in this state, the bonus damage granted by Planar Synergy increases by 1d8 each time you use Requip again after you activate this ability. This state lasts for 1 minute or until you take a turn where you don’t use Requip. Once you enter this state, you must finish a Short or Long rest before you do so again

docs.title: Knight’s Creeds
docs.text: Different orders of arbiters draw their power from various sources of magic. Your choice in creed reflects the order you hail from or the source of your power.

docs.title: Armor of the Giants Bulwark
docs.text: Arbiters who wield the Giant’s Bulwark armors use their strength and resilience to outlast their foes. They specialize in being right in the middle of the battlefield, swinging large weapons at even larger enemies. These Arbiters tend to work in teams with archers and mages, drawing fire, so their allies have space to lay down barrages of arrows and powerful spells.

docs.title: Level 3: Enhanced Armor
docs.text:
You gain access to three Armor Types, which are magical augmentations to whatever armor you are wearing. You have three choices, which get stronger as you increase in level. You can only have one Armor Type active at a time and you choose which type is active when you roll initiative or as an action outside of combat. The three armor types granted by this creed are listed below.

Resilient. If you are hit by an attack, you can use your reaction to reduce the damage by 1d6 + Intelligence Modifier.

Strong.  Any Melee weapon that you are holding gains the Thrown property if it doesn’t have it already. The range for weapons thrown this way is 20/60.

Enforcer. When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you can attempt to Grapple it as part of the same attack. You can Grapple with the same hand that is holding your weapon when you Grapple creatures this way.

docs.title: Level 6: Creed Focus
docs.text: You can goad foes that you strike. Once per turn, when you hit an attack against a creature, you can force it to make a Wisdom saving throw. If the target fails the saving throw, they have Disadvantage on attack rolls against targets other than you until the start of your next turn.

docs.title: Level 9: Improved Armor
docs.text:
Your Armor Types grow in power to match your increase in skill. You gain additional features, benefits, or improvements upon your Armor Types. Previous features do not get replaced, unless stated otherwise.

Resilient. You have an animated barrier that protects you from attacks, granting you a +2 bonus to AC.

Strong. When you hit an attack with a weapon, you can activate the Push weapon mastery property in addition to a different weapon mastery property you are using with that weapon. When you use the Push weapon mastery and push a target into a solid object or another creature, the target takes an additional 1d10 bludgeoning damage.

Enforcer. Whenever you Grapple a creature, that creature has the Restrained condition while Grappled by you.

docs.title: Level 15: Creed Revelation
docs.text: When you finish a Short or Long Rest or when you roll Initiative, you gain a number of Temporary Hit Points equal to two times your Arbiter level.

docs.title: Level 17: Perfected Armor
docs.text:
Each of your Armor Types have reached their pinnacle of power. You gain additional features, benefits, or improvements upon your Armor Types. Previous features do not get replaced, unless stated otherwise.

Resilient. You have resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage as well as one other damage type other than Force of your choice, which is chosen when you equip this armor type.

Strong. Once per turn, if you hit a creature with an attack using a thrown or ranged weapon, you can attempt to pull the target toward you. The target makes a Strength saving throw, on a failed save, it is teleported to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you.

Enforcer. If you are Grappling a creature and you are hit by an attack, you can use your reaction to interpose the Grappled creature between you and the attacker, causing the attack to hit the Grappled creature instead of you.

docs.title: Armor of the Dreadful Duelist
docs.text: Arbiters who wield the Dreadful Duelist armors are excellent at infiltration and trickery. They are often on the side of the underdog, taking out powerful enemies who disparage and harm the innocent. Dreadful Duelists use their enhanced speed and accuracy to strike foes from afar or dash in for the killing blow.

docs.title: Level 3: Enhanced Armor
docs.text:
You gain access to three Armor Types, which are magical augmentations to whatever armor you are wearing. You have three choices, which get stronger as you increase in level. You can only have one Armor Type active at a time and you choose which type is active when you roll initiative or as an action outside of combat. The three armor types granted by this creed are listed below.

Lethal.  After you use Requip, your next weapon attack deals an extra 1d6 Poison damage.

Stealthy. You have Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks. If the Armor you have equipped normally imposes Disadvantage on such checks, the Advantage and Disadvantage cancel each other, as normal.

Precise. Your attack rolls with weapons and Unarmed Strikes can score a Critical Hit on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20.

docs.title: Level 6: Creed Focus
docs.text: You can Dash, Disengage, or Hide as a Bonus action on your turn. Additionally Your Speed increases by 10 feet and your movement is unaffected by non magical Difficult Terrain. You also have a Climb Speed and Swim Speed equal to your walking speed. Your armor does not hinder your ability to swim while this armor type is active.

docs.title: Level 9: Improved Armor
docs.text:
Your Armor Types grow in power to match your increase in skill. You gain additional features, benefits, or improvements upon your Armor Types. Previous features do not get replaced, unless stated otherwise.

Lethal. Once per turn, when you deal Poison damage to a creature, you can force it to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save it takes an and has the Poisoned condition until the end of your next turn.

Stealthy. You can add your Intelligence Modifier to your Dexterity (Stealth) checks.

Precise. After you use Requip, you have Advantage on your next attack roll.

docs.title: Level 15: Creed Revelation
docs.text: Your armor gives you the swiftness to avoid certain dangers. When you're subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw and only half damage if you fail. You can't use this feature if you have the Incapacitated condition.

docs.title: Level 17: Perfected Armor
docs.text:
Each of your Armor Types have reached their pinnacle of power. You gain additional features, benefits, or improvements upon your Armor Types. Previous features do not get replaced, unless stated otherwise.

Lethal. When you deal Poison damage to a creature, you can make that creature Vulnerable to Poison damage for that damage roll. If the creature is already Resistant to Poison damage, it instead loses its Resistance for that damage roll. If it is Immune to Poison damage, it becomes Resistant to Poison damage for that damage roll.

Stealthy. You may gain the Invisible condition as a Bonus Action on your turn. The condition lasts for 1 minute or until you attack or cast a spell.

Precise. When you hit a creature with an attack, you can reduce its Armor Class by 1, to a minimum of 10 + the target’s Dexterity modifier.

docs.title: Armor of the Elemental Emperor
docs.text: Arbiters who wield the Elemental Emperor Armors use elemental magic to enhance their weapons and defensive capabilities. Their elemental enhancements further their ability to adapt to any situation. No matter what enemies they face, the Elemental Emperor has a tool to cut them down.

docs.title: Level 3: Enhanced Armor
docs.text:
You gain access to three Armor Types, which are magical augmentations to whatever armor you are wearing. You have three choices, which get stronger as you increase in level. You can only have one Armor Type active at a time and you choose which type is active when you roll initiative or as an action outside of combat. The three armor types granted by this creed are listed below.

Flame. Your melee weapons deal an extra 1d4 Fire damage.

Earth.        When you take the attack action on your turn, you can replace one of your attacks with an earth quaking stomp that topples enemies. Each creature within 10 feet of you that you choose must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take bludgeoning damage equal to 1d6 + your Intelligence modifier and fall prone.

Storm. When you make a ranged attack with a throw or ranged weapon, you can choose to do Lightning damage instead of the weapon's normal damage type. You ignore the loading property of any weapon if it has it, and if the weapon lacks ammunition, it produces its own when you make an attack with it. The ammunition created by the weapon vanishes the instant after it hits or misses a target.

docs.title: Level 6: Creed Focus
docs.text: When a creature within 60 feet of you that you can see makes an attack against you, you can take a Reaction and deal damage to them equal to your 1d6 + Intelligence modifier. The damage type is determined by the armor type that is currently active: Fire damage for Flame, Bludgeoning damage for Earth, and Lightning damage for Storm.

docs.title: Level 9: Improved Armor
docs.text:
Your Armor Types grow in power to match your increase in skill. You gain additional features, benefits, or improvements upon your Armor Types. Previous features do not get replaced, unless stated otherwise.

Flame. Your melee weapons deal an extra 2d4 Fire damage, instead of 1d4.

Earth. When you take the attack action on your turn, you can replace one of your attacks with conjuring a wall of stone. The wall can be up to  6 inches thick, 10 feet high, and 5 feet wide. Alternatively, the wall can be up to 6 inches thick, 5 feet high, and 10 feet wide. If the wall cuts through a creature’s space when it appears, the creature is pushed to one side of the wall. The wall has an AC of 17 and 15 hit points. It has Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage. You can have a number of these walls active equal to your Proficiency Bonus. If you create a wall after you have the maximum amount active, the oldest wall created is destroyed, otherwise the walls last until they are destroyed.

Storm. Once per turn, when you make a ranged attack with a thrown or ranged weapon, you can repeat the attack against another creature within 30 feet of the original target and within the range of your weapon.

docs.title: Level 15: Creed Revelation
docs.text: You can cast Conjure Minor Elementals as a 5th-level spell. When you cast this spell in this way, you can perform the somatic component while holding weapons or a shield in one or both hands. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for these spells. Once cast this spell using this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long rest.

docs.title: Level 17: Perfected Armor
docs.text:
Each of your Armor Types have reached their pinnacle of power. You gain additional features, benefits, or improvements upon your Armor Types. Previous features do not get replaced, unless stated otherwise.

Flame. Your melee attacks deal an extra 3d4 Fire damage, instead of 2d4.

Earth. When you take the attack action on your turn, you can replace one of your attacks with an earthen grasp. One creature that you can see within 30 feet must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, the target takes Bludgeoning damage equal to 2d6 + your Intelligence modifier and is restrained by a hand made of stone until the end of your next turn. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage and isn’t restrained. The creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns. On a successful save it breaks free.

Storm. Once per turn when you hit a creature with a ranged attack using a thrown or ranged weapon, you can attempt to immobilize the creature as lightning binds it to the ground. The target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save the target’s speed becomes 0 until the end of your next turn.

docs.title: Armor of the Planar Warden
docs.text: Arbiters who wield the Planar Warden Armors connect to the higher planes of Order, Divinity, and Chaos to protect their allies and hold the line against extraplanar threats. They use their powers to fend off invaders from other realms and keep their realm safe. Orders of these Arbiters will often work with Paladins, Wizards, and Clerics to establish wards and armies to contain and prevent extraplanar entities from seizing the Material Plane.

docs.title: Level 3: Enhanced Armor
docs.text:
You gain access to three Armor Types, which are magical augmentations to whatever armor you are wearing. You have three choices, which get stronger as you increase in level. You can only have one Armor Type active at a time and you choose which type is active when you roll initiative or as an action outside of combat. The three armor types granted by this creed are listed below.

Chaos. Once per turn, when you make an attack roll with Advantage, you can force the target to subtract 1d4 from the next saving throw it makes before the end of your next turn, provided that the attack hits it.

Divinity. Once per turn, when you hit a creature while you are within 10 feet of one of your allies, you can deal an extra 1d8 Radiant or Necrotic damage (your choice) to the target.

Order. Once per turn, when you make an attack roll with a weapon, you can forgo rolling the d20 to get an 8 on the die.

docs.title: Level 6: Creed Focus
docs.text: You can temporarily traverse the planes to reposition yourself. As a Bonus Action, you can teleport to an unoccupied space you can see within a number of feet equal to 5 times your Arbiter level. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier and regain all uses when you finish a Long Rest.

docs.title: Level 9: Improved Armor
docs.text:
Your Armor Types grow in power to match your increase in skill. You gain additional features, benefits, or improvements upon your Armor Types. Previous features do not get replaced, unless stated otherwise.

Chaos. When you Requip, you can choose to switch to a random Weapon Set in your Armory, rather than choosing. When you do you, you have Advantage on your next attack roll made with the randomly chosen weapons in that set. Use a dice or other random selection tool to determine which Weapon Set you switch to, assigning each Weapon Set that is currently in your Armory the same probability.

Divinity. Once per turn, when you deal Radiant or Necrotic damage to a creature, you can mark them until the start of your turn. While marked, the next attack made against the target gains a 1d4 bonus to the attack roll. The mark ends early if the target is hit by an attack.

Order. When you miss an attack roll, you gain a +1 bonus to the next attack roll you make before the end of your next turn.

docs.title: Level 15: Creed Revelation
docs.text: You can cast Banishing Smite as a 5th-level spell. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for this spell. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long rest.

docs.title: Level 17: Perfected Armor
docs.text:
Each of your Armor Types have reached their pinnacle of power. You gain additional features, benefits, or improvements upon your Armor Types. Previous features do not get replaced, unless stated otherwise.

Chaos. Once per turn, when you score a Critical Hit with a weapon attack, you can choose to unleash a Wild Magic Surge. Roll on the Wild Magic Surge table from the Sorcerer class to determine the effect.

Divinity. Once per turn, when you deal Radiant or Necrotic damage to a creature, you may gain 10 Temporary Hit Points.

Order.  No attack roll can have Advantage against you unless you have the Incapacitated condition.

docs.title: Necromancer
docs.text:
Necromancer

Necromancers are the defilers of the sanctified, the disturbers of the restful, the horrors of the faith, the fanatics of the arts. Necromancers are the antithesis of all in the world, and no Necromancer is ever truly an ally to any but themselves and their thralls. Truly, it is in a Necromancer’s nature to be against nature, to strive for greater power when all others fail them.

NOTE: The Necromancer class was designed to operate as a replacement to the Animate Dead spell. Characters using the Necromancer class are not expected to have access to Animate Dead. If a character multiclasses and has the ability to learn Animate Dead, talk with your DM to see if it is okay to use alongside the Necromancer class. Otherwise, players with Necromancer levels cannot cast Animate Dead.

docs.title: Becoming A Necromancer…
docs.text:
As a 1st Level Character

  • Gain all the traits in the Core Necromancer Traits table.
  • Gain the Necromancer’s level 1 features, which are listed in the Necromancer Features Table.

As a Multiclass Character

  • Gain the Hit Point Die from the Core Necromancer Traits table.

Level 1: Necromancy

You have an innate affinity for death and reanimation, which manifests as a pool of Necromantic Command. You have 1 Necromantic Command, and you gain more as you reach higher levels, as shown in the Necromantic Command column of the Necromancer Features table. Your Necromantic Command resets to the number shown in the table for your level when you finish a Long Rest (if you have more than this number, it decreases to that number).

You can use your Necromantic Command to fuel the options below, along with other features, such as Reanimate, that use those points.

  • Grave Sight. As a Bonus Action, you may spend 1 Necromantic Command to be able to briefly see through solid objects within a number of feet equal to 5 times your Necromancer level for 1 minute. This sight only enables you to see nonliving, organic remains and gives you Darkvision if you don’t already have it within that range.
  • Minor Minion. As a Magic Action, you may spend 1 Necromantic Command to cast Find Familiar without Material components, creating a familiar with the special form of either a Skeleton or a Zombie (see Appendix B in the Player’s Handbook for the familiar’s stat block). When you cast the spell in this way, the familiar is Undead and disappears when you finish a Long Rest. Additionally, when you take the Attack action, you can forgo one of your own attacks to allow your familiar to make one attack of its own with its Reaction.
  • Whispers of the Damned. As a Magic Action, you may spend 1 Necromantic Command to add your proficiency modifier to one skill or tool with which you lack proficiency. You retain this proficiency for 1 hour or until you use this ability again.

Level 1: Spellcasting

You have learned to cast spells through dedication to dark magic. See chapter 7 for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Necromancer spells, which appear on the Necromancer spell list later in the class’s description.

Cantrips. You know three cantrips of your choice from the Necromancer spell list. Spare the Dying, Toll the Dead, and Thaumaturgy are recommended.

Whenever you gain a Necromancer level, you can replace one of your cantrips with another cantrip of your choice from the Necromancer spell list.

When you reach Necromancer levels 4 and 10, you learn another cantrip of your choice from the Necromancer spell list, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Necromancer Features table.

Spell Slots. The Necromancer Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.

Prepared Spells of Level 1+.  You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two level 1 spells from the Necromancer spell list. Bless, Cure Wounds, Inflict Wounds and Mage Armor are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Necromancer levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Necromancer Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional spells from the Necromancer spell list until the number of spells on your list matches the number on the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you’re a level 3 Necromancer, your list of prepared spells can include six spells of levels 1 and 2 in any combination.

If another Necromancer feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don’t count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Necromancer spells for you.

Changing Your Prepared Spells. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change your list of prepared spells, replacing any of the spells there with other Necromancer spells for which you have spell slots.

Spellcasting Ability. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Necromancer spells.

Spellcasting Focus. You can use an Arcane Focus as a Spellcasting Focus for your Necromancer spells.

Level 2: Reanimate

As a Magic Action, you may spend one or more Necromantic Command to reanimate the organic remains of a corpse or pile of bones you can see within a number of feet equal to 5 times your Necromancer level. The number of Necromantic Command you spend depends on the challenge rating of the creature you attempt to reanimate, as seen in the table below (to the right).

CR Command 0 1 1/8 2 1/4 2 1/2 3 1 4 2 5 3 7 4 8 5 10 6 12 7 14 8 16 9 18 10 20

When you reanimate a creature in this way, you may choose to teleport it to an empty space within 5 feet of you. The creature rises under your control as an Undead Servant until you finish a Long Rest, after which the magic animating it ends and the Servant collapses, lifeless until reanimated once more. While under your control, The Servant obeys your spoken commands and takes its turns in combat immediately after yours. The maximum number of Undead Servants you can have under your control in this way is equal to your proficiency bonus. If you attempt to create an Undead Servant beyond this maximum, the oldest Servant created this way collapses.

When you summon an Undead Servant in this way, it is revived with changes according to the table below. Depending on whether you animated a corpse or a pile of bones will add additional changes.

Level 3: Necromancy Subclass

You gain a Necromancer subclass of your choice. Doctrine of Animation, Doctrine of Death, Doctrine of Life, and Doctrine of Mediation subclasses are detailed after this class’s description. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Necromancer levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass’s features that are of your Necromancer level or lower.

Level 4: Ability Score Improvement

You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Necromancer levels 8, 12, and 16.

Level 5: Soul Reaping

When a creature within 30 feet dies, you may use your reaction to choose a creature other than yourself within 30 feet of you and roll a number of d8s equal to your proficiency modifier. Choose an effect:

  • Heal. The chosen creature regains hit points equal to the result.
  • Harm. The chosen creature makes a Constitution Saving Throw, taking an amount of Necrotic damage equal to the result on a failure.

You can use this ability twice and regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

Level 6: Spirit Calling

Spirit Command Specter 5 Poltergeist 6 Ghost 9

As a Magic Action, you may spend one or more Necromantic Command to summon a spirit. The number of Command you spend depends on the type of spirit you summon, as seen in the table below (to the right). The spirit appears in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you under your control as an Undead Servant until you finish a Long Rest, after which it fades away.  The Servant obeys your spoken commands and takes its turn in combat immediately after yours.

Each Servant created this way counts toward your maximum number of Undead Servants in your Reanimate. If a spirit Undead Servant would collapse, it disappears, instead.

Level 10: Putrefying Presence

Allied Undead within 10 feet of you gain a bonus to melee damage rolls equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1). A creature can benefit from this feature from only one Necromancer at a time.

Level 13: Bone Shields

When a creature within 30 feet of you is hit by an attack, you may use your Reaction and spend 1 Necromantic Command to give that creature resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage until the start of its next turn. 

Level 17: Immortal Form

Your mastery over necromantic magic has changed your body, granting you with supernatural features, whether or not you wish to have them. Necromancy has taken its toll upon you, and devotion to its doctrines has made a claim on your life.

  • Rejuvenation. You gain a small nonmagical vessel for your soul. When you die, your soul may call upon it and your body turns to dust and is slowly reformed within 5 feet of your vessel over the course of 1d10 days. When it finishes reforming, you are brought back to life with all your hit points.  If your vessel is destroyed when you die or before your body finishes reforming, you are not revived. If your vessel is destroyed or misplaced while you’re alive, through an intense magical ritual lasting over the span of 10 minutes, you may spend a 9th level spell slot and 500 GP to destroy your previous vessel and reform a new vessel in an empty space within 5 feet of you.
  • Timelessness. You no longer age. Depending on the nature of your necromantic power, your apparent age is either stagnant or continues to deteriorate to the point of apparent undeath (you choose when you gain this feature).
  • Unlife. You are Resistant to Cold damage, Lightning damage, and Necrotic damage, and Immune to Poison damage, Exhaustion, and Poisoned.

Level 18: Bone Splinters

When you use your Reanimate to create an Undead Servant, its bones reshape around it to provide it newfound protection. The Servant’s Armor Class increases by 1. In addition, when it is hit by a melee attack, it may use its reaction to deal 4 piercing damage to that creature.

Level 19: Epic Boon

You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Recovery is recommended.

Level 20: Archlich

  • You have Truesight to a range of 120 feet
  • You have Advantage on saving throws made to resist or avoid the following conditions: Charmed, Paralyzed, Petrified, and Stunned.
  • You have Proficiency with Constitution saving throws.
  • You are Immune to Necrotic damage.

docs.title: Doctrine of Animation
docs.text:
Raise and amass

Necromancers who follow the Doctrine of Animation are often considered to thirst for power more than any other, sacrificing their life force to create greater and greater armies, to control stronger and stronger creatures. Some of these Necromancers follow Myrkul, some follow Orcus, some follow a king, and others follow simply their own ambition.

Level 3: Animation Doctrine Spells

Your devotion to this doctrine domain ensures you always have certain spells ready. When you reach a Necromancer level specified in the Animation Doctrine Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

Animation Doctrine Spells

Necromancer Level Prepared Spells 3 Command, Unseen Servant, Aid, Locate Object 5 Corpse Explosion, Summon Undead 7 Death Ward, Stone Shape 9 Antilife Shell, Circle of Power

Level 3: Sacrifice

As a Bonus Action, you can expend a spell slot to gain a number of Necromantic Command equal to the slot’s level. You can use this ability once and regain the ability to spend a spell slot in this way when you finish a Long Rest.

Level 7: Hideous Servants

When you use your Reanimate to create an Undead Servant, you may have it exude a noxious stench. When a creature starts its turn within 10 feet of your Undead Servants with this noxious stench, that creature must make a Constitution Saving Throw against your Spell Save DC or be Poisoned until the start of its next turn.  Additionally, you may use your Bonus Action to command an Undead Servant of yours that you can see within 120 feet to use its Reaction to make an attack.

Level 14: Instant Servants

When a creature you can see within range of your Reanimate dies and leaves behind organic remains, you may use your reaction to immediately use your Reanimate on that creature’s remains.

Level 14: Recycling

When one of your Undead Servants you can see within 120 feet of you dies, you may call upon your mystic connection to it (no action required) to regain a number of Necromantic Command equal to half the Command spent to animate the Servant (rounded down). Once you use this feature, you can’t call upon your mystic connection in this way until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

docs.title: Doctrine of Death
docs.text:
Pain and suffering

Few live lives as dismal and empty as the followers of the Doctrine of Death. Truly, there is no greater torment than life, and many devotees of this doctrine believe they relieve the living of the bounds of living. Some devotees, however, deliver unto others their own misery, dragging society down as they themselves shall be dragged down to eternal punishment.

Level 3: Death Doctrine Spells

Your devotion to this doctrine ensures you always have certain spells ready. When you reach a Necromancer level specified in the Death Doctrine Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

Death Doctrine Spells

Necromancer Level Prepared Spells 3 Hex, Inflict Wounds, Blindness/Deafness, Ray of Enfeeblement 5 Bestow Curse, Vampiric Touch 7 Blight, Fire Shield 9 Contagion, Destructive Wave

Level 3: Hands of Harm

As a Magic Action, you may spend one or more Necromantic Command to cast Inflict Wounds without spending a spell slot. When you do, treat the spell as if it was cast in a spell slot of level equal to the amount of Command spent this way. The maximum number of Command you can spend each time you use this ability is equal to half your Necromancer level, rounded up.

Additionally, whenever you cast a spell of 1st level or higher that deals Necrotic damage, you may gain a number of temporary hit points equal to your Necromancer level.[a]

Level 7: Withering Touch

Spells you cast ignore Resistance to Necrotic damage. In addition, when you roll a 1 or 2 on a damage die for a spell that deals Necrotic damage, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll, even if the new roll is a 1 or a 2.

Level 14: Surge of Death

As a Magic Action, you may send a surge of deadly energy out in a 30-foot Emanation. Each creature of your choice the area must make a Constitution saving throw or take 6d6 Necrotic damage and have Disadvantage on attack rolls until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, creatures take half as much damage only.

You can use this ability twice and regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

docs.title: Doctrine of Life
docs.text:
Save the ones you love

There once was a Necromancer lord who was powerful in magic and might. He discovered the key to immortality, and was stricken with the knowledge that those he loved would perish where he was cursed to live forever. Devotees of the Doctrine of Life rarely choose the Doctrine because they want it but instead because they need it. These Necromancers yearn to preserve not their own life, but instead the lives of all those who may suffer and die that the Necromancer alone can truly save.

Level 3: Hands of Healing

As a Magic Action, you may spend one or more Necromantic Command to cast Cure Wounds without spending a spell slot. When you do, treat the spell as if it was cast in a spell slot of level equal to the amount of Command spent this way. The maximum number of Command you can spend each time you use this ability is equal to half your Necromancer level, rounded up.

In addition, when you cast a spell of 1st level or higher that targets a single creature, you may have another creature that you can see within 30 feet of you use its reaction to move up to half its movement speed without provoking opportunity attacks.

Level 3: Life Doctrine Spells

Your devotion to this doctrine ensures you always have certain spells ready. When you reach a Necromancer level specified in the Life Doctrine Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

Life Doctrine Spells

Necromancer Level Prepared Spells 3 Cure Wounds, Sanctuary, Lesser Restoration, Warding Bond 5 Beacon of Hope, Revivify 7 Aura of Life,  Death Ward 9 Mass Cure Wounds, Raise Dead

Level 7: Revitalizing Touch

When you cast a spell with a range of touch that restores hit points to a creature, you may end one condition on it: Blinded, Deafened, Paralyzed, or Poisoned. In addition, when you roll a 1 or 2 when healing a creature with a spell with a range of touch, you can reroll the die and must use the new roll, even if the new roll is a 1 or a 2.

Level 14: Surge of Life

As a Magic Action, you may send a surge of rejuvenating energy out in a 30-foot Emanation. Each creature of your choice in your Emanation gains 6d6 hit points and has advantage on attack rolls until the start of your next turn.

You can use this ability twice and regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

docs.title: Doctrine of Mediation
docs.text:
The bridge between worlds

Mediums come in many forms, but all hear voices, the chilling voices of the deceased that scream out in fear, beg to speak aloud their final words, roar in rage of betrayal, and desperately warn of the horrors of the afterlife. Mediums hear the echoes of the shadowfell, the cries of misery and emptiness that fill the darkness of death. Mediums have learned to call upon these spirits, whether by negotiation or by force, to bestow unto the spirits a new purpose upon the world.

Level 3: Ancient Wisdom

As a Magic Action, you may spend 2 Necromantic Command. When you do, for the next 1 minute, you add your proficiency modifier to all checks made with skills or tools with which you lack proficiency.

Level 3: Mediation Doctrine Spells

Your devotion to this doctrine ensures you always have certain spells ready. When you reach a Necromancer level specified in the Mediation Doctrine Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

Mediation Doctrine Spells

Necromancer Level Prepared Spells 3 Detect Magic, Protection from Evil and Good, Augury, Pass Without Trace 5 Speak with Dead, Spirit Guardians 7 Banishment, Guardian of Faith 9 Dispel Evil and Good, Legend Lore

Level 7: Spirit Affinity

When you use your Spirit Calling, you can spend one fewer Command to summon an Undead Servant spirit. Additionally, you can spend 3 Necromantic Command to summon a Shadow in this way.

Level 14: Otherworldly Communion

As a Magic Action, you may spend 5 Necromantic Command to cast Contact Other Plane without spending a spell slot. When you cast this spell this way, you may connect another willing creature to the entity as well, with the creature making the Intelligence saving throw and asking questions (you cannot speak during this time).

Once you use this ability, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

Level 14: Shadow Form

As a Bonus Action, you can spend 5 Necromantic Command to enter a shadowy form for one hour. While in this shadowy form, you are Invisible while in dim light or darkness or until you make an attack roll, deal damage, or cast a spell. You can become invisible again by using a Magic Action while in dim light or darkness. Additionally you can see normally in Magical Darkness out to a distance of 60 feet.

Once you use this ability, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

docs.title: Doctrine of Orthomancy
docs.text:
Charge the frontlines

Level 3: Armor Training

You gain training with Medium armor and Shields.

Level 3: Bone Shaping

You can forge Bone Weapons out of scrap corpses and body parts. When you finish a Long Rest, you can shape a pile of bones into either two Simple melee weapons or one Simple melee weapon and a Shield. The weapons and Shields created by this feature disintegrate back into bone dust if you use this feature again or if the weapon or Shield is farther than 120 feet away from you. You can use the weapons you make with this feature as a Spellcasting focus for your Necromancer spells.

Additionally, when you finish a Long Rest, if you are not wearing armor,  you can shape a pile of bones into a suit of Scale Male Armor. When you do this, the armor forms around your clothing and is automatically equipped. The armor can’t be removed from you against your will. If you doff the armor, it disintegrates back into a pile of bones. While wearing your Bone Armor, you can spend 1 Necromantic command to cast the Shield of Faith spell without expending a spell slot.

Level 3: Orthomancy Doctrine Spells

Your devotion to this doctrine ensures you always have certain spells ready. When you reach a Necromancer level specified in the Life Doctrine Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

Orthomancy Doctrine Spells

Necromancer Level Prepared Spells 3 Shield of Faith, Wrathful Smite, Shatter, Spiritual Weapon 5 Crusader’s Mantle, Elemental Weapon 7 Staggering Smite, Stoneskin 9 Wall of Stone, Animate Objects

Level 7: Drain Strike

When you hit an attack using a Bone Weapon, you can expend one or more Necromantic Command, up to a maximum of your Intelligence modifier. When you do so, you deal an additional 1d6 Necrotic damage for each Command expended. You also regain a number of Hit Points equal to half of the Necrotic damage you deal with this feature.

Level 7: Extra Attack

You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. In addition, you can cast one of your cantrips that has a casting time of an action in place of one of those attacks.

Level 14: Death Blade

The weapons made by your Bone Shaping feature now ooze negative energy. When you hit a creature with a Bone Weapon, you can choose to deal Necrotic damage instead of the weapon’s normal damage type and it deals an additional 1d8 Necrotic damage.

Level 14: Exoskeleton

The armor you create with Bone Shaping is greatly enhanced. You can now choose to create Half Plate Armor instead of Scale Mail Armor. Additionally, your armor no longer imposes Disadvantage on (Dexterity) Stealth checks.

3rd-level Necromancy Spell (Necromancer, Wizard)

Casting Time: Action

Range: 150 feet

Component: V, S, M (a small vial of putrid methane gas or a piece of rotting flesh)

Duration: Instantaneous

You send a concentrated burst of necrotic energy toward a corpse or undead creature you can see within range, causing it to unleash a devastating explosion.

All creatures within a 10 foot Emanation of the target (including the target) must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw as the target explodes, taking 6d8 Force damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
Attachment -This weapon can be attached to any type of crossbow or firearm to allow for melee combat while holding this weapon. The bayonet can be removed to be used similarly to a dagger. Removing the bayonet requires one bonus action. While attached, the bayonet only has the light property if the weapon it is attached to also has that property.

Bundle- You can bundle multiple of these explosives together to increase the damage by 1d6 and area of effect by 5 ft for every additional explosive added. You can have up to 10 explosives in one bundle.

Close Contact- This weapon does not have disadvantage when attacking within 5 feet.

Explosives- As an attack, a creature can light this explosive and throw it to a point within 60 ft. Each creature within the area of effect must make a DC 12 Dexterity saving throw, or take the full damage of the explosive, and half as much on a failure.

Destructive- This weapon does extra damage to objects and structures. When rolling for damage against objects and structures, roll double the amount of damage dice.

Lethal - If this weapon lands a critical hit, roll one extra damage dice when determining the total damage it deals.

Trapping - A Large or smaller creature hit by this weapon is restrained until it is freed. This weapon has no effect on creatures that are formless, or creatures that are Huge or larger. A creature can use its action to make a DC 10 Strength check, freeing itself or another creature within its reach on a success. Dealing 5 slashing damage to the weapon (AC 10) also frees the creature without harming it, ending the effect and destroying the weapon.

Special Reload - The weapon can be fired multiple times before being reloaded. Reloading the weapon requires using one attack from the attack action. If the character using the weapon has the extra attack feature, they can use one attack to reload the weapon and their remaining attacks can be used to fire it.

Fritz’s Fantastical Formulation

Each potion takes one action to drink and lasts for one minute by default. Multiple effects can be combined and modified to create a unique potion experience. Each potion has a number of effects and types of flask. Up to 3 effects can be chosen. Most effects are repeatable, stacking the benefits of each one. For example, using 2 healing effects would cause the potion to heal for 4d8+8. Those that are not repeatable are marked with an asterix (*). Some effects are listed as Debuffs, if an effect is a debuff, the target can try to resist the effect by succeeding on a DC 14 Constitution saving throw. Any debuff that deals damage will deal half damage on a successful save. Different flask types allow the potion to be administered in different ways or allow it to bypass certain restrictions outlined above. If a potion is applied to a blade or piece of ammunition, once one attack hits a target, the whole potion is spent, regardless of how many pieces of ammunition the potion is used on. When a potion is applied on a weapon, it remains stable for one minute, if the potion is not used before that time ends, then the potion is no longer usable and the effects of the potion dissipate.

docs.title: Soul Linked Item
docs.text:
Soul Links

Soul Linked Items are special magical items that are bound to an adventurer early on in their career. These items grow in power with the adventurer and are highly unique, usually acting as manifestations of an adventurer’s personality. If this item is lost, the adventurer must perform an intensive ritual or go on a grand journey to recover it or manifest a new one, the details of such are determined by the manner in which it was lost and the nature of the adventurer who wielded it. When making your Soul Link, pick a magic item type, this can be an Arcane Focus, Armor, Shield, Tool, Wondrous Item, or Weapon. Each magic item type has unique features that can be chosen as the item grows in power.

When you gain a Soul Link, choose a level 1 Manifestation. As you gain levels, so will your Soul Link. At levels 4, 8, 12, 16, and 19, your item will manifest newer and more powerful abilities. When you reach a level where you gain a feature, you can choose any feature that has a level requirement less than or equal to your level. Choose any Manifestation from either the general list (which applies to any type of magical item) or one from the specific list associated with your item type. Also feel free to get creative and suggest a manifestation specific to your item. Any suggestions are subject to DM approval and should generally line up with other manifestation options.

Flavoring your Soul Link

When considering what kind of Soul Link your character has, carefully consider how this item might look, any quirks or oddities that make it unique, how your character acquired such an item, if the item has a history with any previous owners, what it might look or sound like when using its manifestations, what personality traits it has if it is sentient, and so much more. Try to integrate your Soul Link with your character's personality, backstory, and fighting style. Try to go beyond just “I found this sword one day and it has cool powers I guess”. Really dive into features and descriptions that enhance the roleplaying elements of your character. Suggest different abilities that might be unique to your item, think of a colorful description, make up a cool name, or even add curses and disadvantages your character might have to overcome. Get creative and make a magic item that really tells a story.

docs.title: General
docs.text: Manifestations in this list are fairly common and not tied to any specific item type. They can still add flavor to your character, but are just as at home on a suit of armor, as they  are on a dagger, lute, or magic wand.

docs.title: Level 1:
docs.text:

  • The item pulses with your heartbeat, casting warm light or a cold glow. The item emits Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet. You can beckon or snuff out this light as a Bonus Action.
  • Pocket Space
  • While holding the item, you can send it to an extradimensional space as a Bonus Action. You can retrieve the item from the extradimensional space when you roll Initiative or as a Bonus Action. You cannot retrieve the item if you don’t have a free hand to hold it.
  • *Variation for Armor: Retractable
  • You can don and doff this armor as a Bonus Action
  • Disguise
  • As a Bonus Action, you can disguise your item into a similarly sized mundane item. Choose the mundane appearance when you select this feature. While in mundane form, the item doesn't appear magical and only a spell of 2nd level or higher reveals otherwise.
  • Sentience
  • Not all Soul Links are sentient, but it is far from uncommon. A sentient soul link has its own personality that compliments the personality of its wielder, either by encouraging them to stay on the true and right path, or tempting them to wander on the darker roads. Either way, having a sentient Soul Link provides the following benefit:
  • Your Soul Link gains an Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma score. Choose one to start at 8, another to start at 10, and the final to start at 12. Whenever you gain a new manifestation, you can choose to forgo gaining a manifestation to increase one of these scores by 2. Whenever you make a skill check or saving throw using any of these ability scores, you can instead choose to use your soul link’s ability score. Apply any of your proficiencies or class features after changing which ability score you are using.

docs.title: Smithing
docs.text:
Simple - requires no moving parts and is generally one piece of metal shaped quite quickly into form. All simple weapons and some types of armor, like breastplate.

Moderate - requires multiple pieces of metal shaped into a more intricate form. All martial weapons, except certain types, and some armor falls in this category.

Complex - requires lots of pieces and many moving parts. Some martial weapons and most armor belong to this category.

Crafting time

Simple - weight / 4 = # of days needed to craft; minimum 1 day, round up

Moderate - weight / 2 = # of days needed to craft; minimum 1 day, round up

Complex - weight = # of days needed to craft; minimum 1 day, round up

For a few examples, this means that:

Shield (Simple) 6lbs = 2 days of crafting

Scale Mail (Moderate) 45lbs = 23 days of crafting

Ringmail (Complex) 40lbs = 40 days of crafting

But that doesn’t cover it all. Ringmail and Chainmail are highly complex in that they require up to thousands of rings crafted, but the individual rings can be crafted by themselves and so they can use our mini-anvil by a campfire. To determine how big something is, we will have to look at each item on a case-by-case basis and separate them into two categories: Campfire or Forge.

And that category is pretty self explanatory. If something can be crafted at the campfire, it’ll be in the Campfire category, everything else will fall into the Forge category.

So now that we have our different complexities sorted, our different qualities, what can be crafted where, it’s time to figure out Craft DCs. I am going to start with a base DC of 13. I am starting with a base of 13 as I assume blacksmiths have a slightly higher strength, like 12 or 13, and they have a +2 proficiency, which means the average they will get when rolling a d20 over and over again will be 13 (10 base + 2 prof + 1 str). For each level of complexity, we will add 1 to the DC. So Moderate will be DC 14 and Complex will be DC 15.

And then for Masterwork, we will raise the DC by 8 so that Simple is DC 21, Moderate DC 22 & Complex DC 23. My thinking behind that is that when a character is level 20 and retiring as a world famous blacksmith, they will have a +6 proficiency, a (if a strength based character) +5 to their strength. This gives them an average of 21 when they roll a d20. I wouldn’t find it unbelievable for a master craftsmen to have masterwork quality goods on average, since they are known for their amazing quality.

Chain shirt (Complex) 20lbs, 20 days / DC15 - 3 craft checks / cost: 25 gp / Campfire

Plate (Complex) 65lbs, 65 days / DC15 - 10 craft checks / cost: 750 gp / Forge

Scale Mail (Moderate) 45lbs, 23 days / DC14 - 4 craft checks / cost: 25 gp / Campfire

Rapier (Moderate) 2lbs, 1 day / DC14 - 1 craft check / cost: 12 gp 5 sp / Campfire

Masterwork Dagger (Simple) 1lb, 2 days / DC21 - 1 craft check / cost: 3 gp / Campfire

Masterwork Flail (Complex) 2lbs, 2 days / DC23 - 1 craft check / cost: 30 gp / Campfire

Scrap Glaive (Moderate) 6lbs, 3 days / No Check / cost: 10 gp / Forge

Scrap War Pick (Moderate) 2lbs, 1 day / No Check / cost: 2 gp 5 sp / Campfire
